translations.literal: When a ceremony is imminent, the Court of the Imperial Stud's officials who milk mares are ordered to present it in leather bags borne by those who serve the drink.
translations.idiomatic: Before a ceremony, the Court of the Imperial Stud's mare-milking officers are ordered to send it in leather bags borne by those who serve the drink.

sentences.zh: 其馬牲既與三牲同登於俎，而割奠之饌，復與籩豆俱設。

translations.literal: The horse victim is placed on the offering stand together with the three victims, and the food for the cutting and presentation is set out together with the baskets and stands.
translations.idiomatic: The horse victim is placed on the offering stand with the three standard victims, and the food for the cutting and presentation is set out with the baskets and stands.

sentences.zh: 將奠牲盤酹馬湩，則蒙古太祝升詣第一座，呼帝後神諱，以致祭年月日數、牲齊品物，致其祝語。

translations.literal: When about to present the victim tray and libate mare's milk, the Mongol Grand Invoker ascends to the first seat, calls out the taboo names of the emperor and empress, states the year, month, day, and number of the sacrifice, the victims and offerings and their kinds, and delivers the prayer.
translations.idiomatic: When about to present the victim tray and libate mare's milk, the Mongol Grand Invoker ascends to the first seat, calls out the emperor's and empress's taboo names, states the date and details of the sacrifice, victims, and offerings, and delivers the prayer.

sentences.zh: 以次詣列室，皆如之。

translations.literal: He proceeds in order to each chamber, doing the same throughout.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeds in order to each chamber, doing the same throughout.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，則以割奠之余，撒於南欞星門外，名曰拋撒茶飯。

translations.literal: When the rites are finished, the remainder of the cutting and presentation is scattered outside the southern Lattice Star Gate, called the casting forth of tea and food.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites are finished, the remainder of the offerings is scattered outside the southern Lattice Star Gate in what is called the casting forth of tea and food.

sentences.zh: 蓋以國禮行事，尤其所重也。

translations.literal: Because the national rites are observed in conducting affairs, this is especially valued.
translations.idiomatic: Because national custom governs these rites, this observance is especially valued.

sentences.zh: 始至元初，金大祝魏友諒者仕於朝，詣中書言太常寺奉祀宗廟禮不備者數事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhiyuan, Wei Youliang, a Jin Grand Invoker, served at court and went to the Secretariat to say that several matters in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' rites for serving the ancestral temple were incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhiyuan era, Wei Youliang, a Jin Grand Invoker serving at court, told the Secretariat that several matters in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' ancestral temple rites were incomplete.

sentences.zh: 禮部移太常考前代典禮，以勘友諒所言，皆非是，由是禮官代有討論。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites directed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to examine the rituals of earlier dynasties and verify Youliang's statements; none proved correct, and from this the ritual officials have debated generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites directed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to examine earlier dynasties' rituals and verify Youliang's claims; none proved correct, and ritual officials have debated the matter ever since.

sentences.zh: 割奠之禮，初惟太常卿設之。

translations.literal: For the cutting-and-presentation rite, at first only the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set it out.
translations.idiomatic: At first only the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices arranged the cutting-and-presentation rite.

sentences.zh: 桑哥為初獻，乃有三獻等官同設之儀。

translations.literal: When Sangge served as first presenter, there came to be a protocol by which the first, second, and final presenters and other officers all set it out together.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangge served as first presenter, the first, second, and final presenters and other officers were all made to arrange it together.

sentences.zh: 博士議曰：「凡陳設祭品、實樽罍等事，獻官皆不與也，獨此親設之，然後再升殿，恐非誠愨專一之道。

translations.literal: The erudites deliberated, saying: 「In all matters of arranging sacrificial gifts, filling goblets and jars, and the like, the presentation officers do not take part; yet in this alone they set things out in person, then ascend the hall again—this may not be the way of sincere devotion with single-minded focus.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual erudites argued: 「For arranging offerings, filling goblets and jars, and the like, presentation officers normally take no part; yet here they set things out themselves and only then reascend the hall—this hardly accords with sincere, single-minded devotion.

sentences.zh: 且大禮使等官，尤非其職。

translations.literal: Moreover, for officers such as the Commissioner of Great Rites, it is especially not their duty.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for officers such as the Commissioner of Great Rites, it is especially outside their proper duties.

sentences.zh: 」大樂署長言：「割奠之禮，宜別撰樂章。

translations.literal: 」The Director of the Grand Music Office said: 「For the cutting-and-presentation rite, separate music texts ought to be composed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Director of the Grand Music Office said: 「The cutting-and-presentation rite should have its own musical texts.

sentences.zh: 」博士議曰：「三獻之禮，實依古制。

translations.literal: 」The erudites deliberated, saying: 「The three presentations rite truly follows the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: 」The erudites replied: 「The three presentations truly follow ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 若割肉，奠葡萄酒、馬湩，別撰樂章，是又成一獻也。

translations.literal: If cutting meat, presenting grape wine and mare's milk, and composing separate music texts constitute yet another presentation, that would make yet another presentation.
translations.idiomatic: To cut meat, present grape wine and mare's milk, and add separate music would amount to yet another presentation.

sentences.zh: 」又議：「燔膋膟與今燒飯禮合，不可廢。

translations.literal: 」They further deliberated: 「Burning fatty meat and minced flesh accords with the present burning-rice rite and should not be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: 」They added: 「Burning fatty meat and minced flesh matches the present burning-rice rite and should not be dropped.

sentences.zh: 形鹽、糗餌、粉餈、裛食、糝食非古。

translations.literal: Shaped salt, dried grain cakes, powdered cakes, wrapped foods, and mixed grain foods are not of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Shaped salt, dried grain cakes, powdered cakes, wrapped foods, and mixed grain foods are not ancient.

sentences.zh: 雷鼓、路鼓，與播鼗之制不同。

translations.literal: Thunder drums and road drums differ from the system of shaking tambourines.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder drums and road drums differ from the prescribed shaking of tambourines.

sentences.zh: 攝祀大禮使終夕堅立，無其義。

translations.literal: For a surrogate sacrifice the Commissioner of Great Rites stands rigidly throughout the night—there is no propriety in this.
translations.idiomatic: Having the Commissioner of Great Rites stand rigidly all night at a surrogate sacrifice has no proper justification.

sentences.zh: 」知禮者皆有取於其言。

translations.literal: 」Those versed in ritual all found merit in their statements.
translations.idiomatic: 」Those versed in ritual generally approved of what they said.

sentences.zh: 英宗之初，博士又言：「今冬祭即烝也。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Yingzong's reign, the erudites again said: 「The present winter sacrifice is the zheng offering.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Yingzong's reign the erudites again urged: 「The present winter sacrifice is the zheng offering.

sentences.zh: 天子親稞太室，功臣宜配享。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven should personally perform the kuo rite at the Grand Chamber, and meritorious ministers ought to receive paired offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor should personally perform the kuo libation at the Grand Chamber, and meritorious ministers ought to share in the paired offerings.

sentences.zh: 」事亦弗果行。

translations.literal: 」The matter likewise was not carried out in the end.
translations.idiomatic: 」This proposal, too, was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 廟制：至元十七年，新作於大都。

translations.literal: Temple system: in the seventeenth year of Zhiyuan, a new temple was built at Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Temple layout: in Zhiyuan 17 a new Imperial Ancestral Temple was built at Dadu.

sentences.zh: 前廟後寢。

translations.literal: There was a front temple and a rear sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: It had a front temple and a rear sleeping hall.

sentences.zh: 正殿東西七間，南北五間，內分七室。

translations.literal: The main hall was seven bays east to west and five bays north to south, divided within into seven chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall measured seven bays east–west and five north–south, with seven chambers inside.

sentences.zh: 殿陛二成三階，中曰泰階，西曰西階，東曰阼階。

translations.literal: The hall terrace had two tiers and three flights of steps: the center was called the Grand Steps, the west the Western Steps, and the east the Eastern Steps.
translations.idiomatic: The terrace had two tiers and three stairways: the Grand Steps in the center, the Western Steps on the west, and the Eastern Steps on the east.

sentences.zh: 寢殿東西五間，南北三間。

translations.literal: The sleeping hall was five bays east to west and three bays north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The sleeping hall was five bays east–west and three north–south.

sentences.zh: 環以宮城，四隅重屋，號角樓。

translations.literal: It was encircled by a palace wall; at the four corners were double-roofed towers called corner towers.
translations.idiomatic: A palace wall encircled it, with double-roofed corner towers at the four corners.

sentences.zh: 正南、正東、正西宮門三，門各五門，皆號神門。

translations.literal: There were three palace gates on the due south, east, and west; each gate had five doorways, all called Spirit Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Three palace gates faced south, east, and west; each had five doorways, all called Spirit Gates.

sentences.zh: 殿下道直東西神門曰橫街，直南門曰通街，甓之。

translations.literal: Below the hall, the path running straight east and west from the spirit gates was called Cross Street; that running straight south from the gate was called Through Street, and it was paved with brick.
translations.idiomatic: Below the hall, the east–west avenue from the spirit gates was Cross Street; the southward avenue from the gate was Through Street, paved in brick.

sentences.zh: 通街兩旁井二，皆覆以亭。

translations.literal: On either side of Through Street were two wells, each covered by a pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Two wells flanked Through Street, each sheltered by a pavilion.

sentences.zh: 宮城外，繚以崇垣。

translations.literal: Outside the palace wall, a lofty outer wall was built around it.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the palace wall a high outer enclosure was built.

sentences.zh: 饌幕殿七間，在宮城南門之東，南向。

translations.literal: The Feast Pavilion Hall had seven bays, east of the palace's south gate, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Feast Pavilion Hall, seven bays, stood east of the palace south gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 齊班廳五間，在宮城之東南，西向。

translations.literal: The Formation Hall had five bays, southeast of the palace, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Formation Hall, five bays, stood southeast of the palace, facing west.

sentences.zh: 省饌殿一間，在宮城東門少北，南向。

translations.literal: The Inspection of Offerings Hall had one bay, slightly north of the palace east gate, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspection of Offerings Hall, one bay, stood just north of the palace east gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 初獻齋室在宮城之東，東垣門內少北，西向。

translations.literal: The first presenter's fasting chamber was east of the palace, slightly north inside the eastern outer gate, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The first presenter's fasting chamber lay east of the palace, just inside the eastern outer gate and slightly to the north, facing west.

sentences.zh: 其南為亞終獻、司徒、大禮使、助奠、七祀獻官等齋室，皆西向。

translations.literal: South of it were fasting chambers for the second and final presenters, the Minister of Education, the Commissioner of Great Rites, the assistant in presentation, the presentation officers for the seven sacrifices, and the like—all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: South of it were fasting chambers for the second and final presenters, the Minister of Education, the Commissioner of Great Rites, assistants in presentation, officers for the seven sacrifices, and others—all facing west.

sentences.zh: 雅樂庫在宮城西南，東向。

translations.literal: The Ceremonial Music Storehouse was southwest of the palace, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Music Storehouse stood southwest of the palace, facing east.

sentences.zh: 法物庫、儀鸞庫在宮城之東北，皆南向。

translations.literal: The Ritual Objects Storehouse and the Ceremonial Insignia Storehouse were northeast of the palace, both facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Objects and Ceremonial Insignia storehouses stood northeast of the palace, both facing south.

sentences.zh: 都監局在其東少南，西向。

translations.literal: The Directorate Office was slightly southeast of them, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate Office lay slightly southeast of them, facing west.

sentences.zh: 東垣之內，環築墻垣為別院。

translations.literal: Within the eastern outer wall, walls were built in a ring to form a separate compound.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the eastern outer wall a walled compound was built as a separate courtyard.

sentences.zh: 內神廚局五間，在北，南向。

translations.literal: The Inner Spirit Kitchen Office had five bays, on the north side, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Spirit Kitchen Office, five bays, stood on the north side of the compound, facing south.

sentences.zh: 井在神廚之東北，有亭。

translations.literal: A well was northeast of the spirit kitchen, with a pavilion over it.
translations.idiomatic: A well northeast of the spirit kitchen had a pavilion over it.

sentences.zh: 酒庫三間，在井亭南，西向。

translations.literal: The wine storehouse had three bays, south of the well pavilion, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The wine storehouse, three bays, stood south of the well pavilion, facing west.

sentences.zh: 祠祭局三間，對神廚局，北向。

translations.literal: The Sacrificial Offerings Office had three bays, opposite the spirit kitchen, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrificial Offerings Office, three bays, faced the spirit kitchen across the courtyard, facing north.

sentences.zh: 院門西向。

translations.literal: The compound gate faced west.
translations.idiomatic: The compound gate faced west.

sentences.zh: 百官廚五間，在神廚院南，西向。

translations.literal: The Officials' Kitchen had five bays, south of the spirit kitchen compound, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Officials' Kitchen, five bays, stood south of the spirit kitchen compound, facing west.

sentences.zh: 宮城之南，復為門，與中神門相值，左右連屋六十餘間，東掩齊班廳，西值雅樂庫，為諸執事齋房。

translations.literal: South of the palace wall another gate was built, aligned with the central spirit gate; to left and right more than sixty connected rooms extended—on the east covering the Formation Hall, on the west facing the Ceremonial Music Storehouse—serving as fasting rooms for all attending officers.
translations.idiomatic: South of the palace wall another gate aligned with the central spirit gate; more than sixty linked rooms to either side—the east wing covering the Formation Hall and the west facing the Ceremonial Music Storehouse—served as fasting rooms for attending officers.

sentences.zh: 築崇墉以環其外，東西南開欞星門三，門外馳道，抵齊化門之通衢。

translations.literal: A lofty wall was built to encircle the outside; three Lattice Star Gates were opened on the east, south, and west, and outside the gates an imperial roadway ran to the main thoroughfare of Qihua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A high outer wall encircled the complex; Lattice Star Gates opened east, south, and west, with an imperial roadway outside leading to the Qihua Gate thoroughfare.

sentences.zh: 神主：至元三年，始命太保劉秉忠考古制為之，高一尺二寸，上頂圜徑二寸八分，四廂合剡一寸一分。

translations.literal: Spirit tablets: in the third year of Zhiyuan, the Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong was first ordered to examine the ancient system and make them—one foot two inches high, the rounded top two inches eight fen in diameter, the four sides together beveled one inch one fen.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit tablets: in Zhiyuan 3 Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong was first ordered to study the ancient model and fashion them—one foot two inches tall, with a rounded top two inches eight fen across and sides beveled one inch one fen in all.

sentences.zh: 上下四方穿，中央通孔，徑九分，以光漆題尊謚於背上。

translations.literal: Holes were bored through top and bottom and the four sides, with a central bore nine fen in diameter; posthumous titles of honor were inscribed on the back in bright lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: Holes pierced top, bottom, and four sides, with a central bore nine fen wide; posthumous titles were inscribed on the back in bright lacquer.

sentences.zh: 匱趺底蓋俱方。

translations.literal: The case, base, bottom, and lid were all square.
translations.idiomatic: Case, base, bottom, and lid were all square.

sentences.zh: 底自下而上，蓋從上而下。

translations.literal: The bottom fitted on from below; the lid fitted on from above.
translations.idiomatic: The bottom was fitted from below; the lid from above.

sentences.zh: 底齊趺，方一尺，厚三寸。

translations.literal: The bottom was flush with the base—one foot square and three inches thick.
translations.idiomatic: The bottom was flush with the base: one foot square and three inches thick.

sentences.zh: 皆準元祐古尺圖。

translations.literal: All measurements followed the Yuanyou ancient-foot diagram.
translations.idiomatic: All dimensions followed the Yuanyou-era standard-foot chart.

sentences.zh: 主及匱趺皆用栗木，匱趺並用玄漆，設祏室以安奉。

translations.literal: Both tablet and case-base were of chestnut wood; case and base were both finished in black lacquer, and a collateral shrine was established for their installation.
translations.idiomatic: Tablet and case-base were chestnut wood, case and base finished in black lacquer, and a collateral shrine was set up to receive them.

sentences.zh: 帝主用曲幾，黃羅帕覆之。

translations.literal: For an emperor's tablet a curved armrest was used, covered with a yellow silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: An emperor's tablet used a curved armrest and was covered with yellow silk.

sentences.zh: 後主用直幾，紅羅帕覆之；

translations.literal: For an empress's tablet a straight armrest was used, covered with a red silk cloth;
translations.idiomatic: An empress's tablet used a straight armrest and was covered with red silk;

sentences.zh: 祏室，每室紅錦厚褥一，紫錦薄褥一，黃羅復帳一，龜背紅簾一，緣以黃羅帶飾。

translations.literal: in the collateral shrine, each chamber had one thick red brocade cushion, one thin purple brocade cushion, one yellow silk canopy, one tortoise-shell-pattern red curtain, and trim of yellow silk ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: each collateral chamber had one thick red brocade cushion, one thin purple brocade cushion, one yellow silk canopy, one tortoise-shell-pattern red curtain, and yellow silk ribbon trim.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月十八日，國師奉旨造木質金表牌位十有六，亦號神主。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the twelfth month of the sixth year, the state preceptor received an order to make sixteen wooden plaques with gilded faces, also called spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day of the twelfth month of year 6 the state preceptor was ordered to make sixteen wooden plaques with gilded faces, also termed spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 設大榻金椅位，置祏室前。

translations.literal: A great couch with golden chairs was set up before the collateral shrine.
translations.idiomatic: A great couch with golden chairs was placed before the collateral shrine.

sentences.zh: 帝位於右，後位於左，題號其面，籠以銷金絳紗，其制如櫝。

translations.literal: The emperor's seat was on the right and the empress's on the left; titles were inscribed on the face, and they were cased in gilded crimson gauze in the form of coffers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's seat stood on the right and the empress's on the left, with titles on the face; each was encased in gilded crimson gauze like a coffer.

sentences.zh: 祝有二：祝冊，親祀用之。

translations.literal: Prayers were of two kinds: prayer slips, used when the emperor sacrificed in person.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer texts came in two forms: prayer slips, used when the emperor sacrificed in person.

sentences.zh: 制以竹，每副二十有四簡，貫以紅絨絳。

translations.literal: They were made of bamboo; each set had twenty-four slips strung on red floss cord.
translations.idiomatic: They were bamboo; each set had twenty-four slips threaded on red floss.

sentences.zh: 面用膠粉塗飾，背飾以絳金綺。

translations.literal: The face was coated with glue and powder; the back was decorated with crimson brocade with gold.
translations.idiomatic: The face was coated with glue and powder; the back lined with gold-patterned crimson brocade.

sentences.zh: 藏以楠木縷金雲龍匣。

translations.literal: They were stored in a nanwood case with gold cloud-dragon tracery.
translations.idiomatic: They were kept in a nanwood case inlaid with gold cloud-dragon designs.

sentences.zh: 塗金鎖鑰，韜以紅錦囊，蒙以銷金雲龍絳羅覆。

translations.literal: Gilded locks and keys secured them; they were wrapped in a red brocade pouch and covered with gilded cloud-dragon crimson gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Gilded locks secured them; they were wrapped in a red brocade pouch and covered with gilded cloud-dragon crimson gauze.

sentences.zh: 擬撰祝文、書祝、讀祝，皆翰林詞臣掌之。

translations.literal: Drafting prayer texts, writing them out, and reading them were all managed by Hanlin academicians.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting, writing, and reading the prayer texts were all handled by Hanlin academicians.

sentences.zh: 至大二年親祀，竹冊長一尺二寸，廣一寸二分，厚三分。

translations.literal: For the personal sacrifice in the second year of Zhida, the bamboo slips were one foot two inches long, one inch two fen wide, and three fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: At the personal sacrifice in Zhida 2, each bamboo slip was one foot two inches long, one inch two fen wide, and three fen thick.

sentences.zh: 至治二年正月親祀，竹冊八副，每冊二十有四簡，長一尺一寸，廣一寸，厚一分二厘。

translations.literal: For the personal sacrifice in the first month of the second year of Zhizhi, there were eight sets of bamboo slips; each set had twenty-four slips one foot one inch long, one inch wide, and one fen two li thick.
translations.idiomatic: At the personal sacrifice in the first month of Zhizhi 2 there were eight bamboo sets of twenty-four slips each, one foot one inch long, one inch wide, and one fen two li thick.

sentences.zh: 祝版，攝祀用之，制以楸木，長二尺四寸，廣一尺二寸，厚一分。

translations.literal: Prayer boards, used for surrogate sacrifice, were made of catalpa wood, two feet four inches long, one foot two inches wide, and one fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer boards for surrogate sacrifice were catalpa wood, two feet four inches long, one foot two inches wide, and one fen thick.

sentences.zh: 其面背飾以精潔楮紙。

translations.literal: Front and back were decorated with fine clean paper.
translations.idiomatic: Both faces were lined with fine, clean paper.

sentences.zh: 祝文，至元時，享於太祖室，稱孝孫嗣皇帝臣某；

translations.literal: Prayer formulas: in the Zhiyuan period, when offering at Taizu's chamber, one styled oneself "the filial grandson, the succeeding emperor, your subject So-and-so";
translations.idiomatic: Prayer formulas: under Zhiyuan, when offering at Taizu's chamber one wrote as "the filial grandson, succeeding emperor, your subject [name]";

sentences.zh: 睿宗室，稱孝子嗣皇帝臣某。

translations.literal: at Ruizong's chamber, one styled oneself "the filial son, the succeeding emperor, your subject So-and-so."
translations.idiomatic: at Ruizong's chamber as "the filial son, succeeding emperor, your subject [name]."

sentences.zh: 天歷時，享自太祖至裕宗四室，皆稱孝曾孫嗣皇帝臣某；

translations.literal: In the Tianli period, when offering from Taizu through Yuzong's four chambers, all styled themselves "the filial great-grandson, the succeeding emperor, your subject So-and-so";
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianli era, offerings from Taizu through Yuzong's four chambers all used "the filial great-grandson, succeeding emperor, your subject [name]";

sentences.zh: 順宗室，稱孝孫嗣皇帝臣某；

translations.literal: at Shunzong's chamber, one styled oneself "the filial grandson, the succeeding emperor, your subject So-and-so";
translations.idiomatic: at Shunzong's chamber as "the filial grandson, succeeding emperor, your subject [name]";

sentences.zh: 成宗至英宗三室，皆稱嗣皇帝臣某；

translations.literal: for the three chambers from Chengzong through Yingzong, all styled themselves "the succeeding emperor, your subject So-and-so";
translations.idiomatic: for Chengzong through Yingzong's three chambers simply "succeeding emperor, your subject [name]";

sentences.zh: 武宗室，稱孝子嗣皇帝臣某。

translations.literal: at Wuzong's chamber, one styled oneself "the filial son, the succeeding emperor, your subject So-and-so."
translations.idiomatic: at Wuzong's chamber as "the filial son, succeeding emperor, your subject [name]."

sentences.zh: 幣：以白繒為之，每段長一丈八尺。

translations.literal: Silk offerings: made of white silk, each piece one zhang eight chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Silk offerings were white silk, each piece one zhang eight chi long.

sentences.zh: 牲齊庶品：大祀，馬一，用色純者，有副；

translations.literal: Victims, offerings, and miscellaneous goods for great sacrifice: one horse of pure color, with a spare;
translations.idiomatic: Victims and offerings for a great sacrifice: one horse of uniform color, with a spare;

sentences.zh: 牛一，其角握，其色赤，有副；

translations.literal: one ox whose horns were cupped in the hand, of red color, with a spare;
translations.idiomatic: one ox with horns cupped in the hand, red in color, with a spare;

sentences.zh: 羊，其色白；

translations.literal: sheep of white color;
translations.idiomatic: sheep, white in color;

sentences.zh: 豕，其色黑；

translations.literal: swine of black color;
translations.idiomatic: swine, black in color;

sentences.zh: 鹿。

translations.literal: and deer.
translations.idiomatic: and deer.

sentences.zh: 凡馬、牛、羊、豕、鹿牲體，每室七盤，單室五盤。

translations.literal: For the flesh of horse, ox, sheep, swine, and deer as victims, each chamber had seven trays; a single chamber had five trays.
translations.idiomatic: Portions of horse, ox, sheep, swine, and deer were set out in seven trays per chamber, or five for a single chamber.

sentences.zh: 太羹，每室三登；

translations.literal: Plain broth: three tureens per chamber;
translations.idiomatic: Plain broth: three tureens per chamber;

sentences.zh: 和羹，每室三铏。

translations.literal: seasoned broth: three cauldrons per chamber.
translations.idiomatic: seasoned broth: three cauldrons per chamber.

sentences.zh: 籩之實，每室十有二品；

translations.literal: The contents of the basket stands: twelve kinds per chamber;
translations.idiomatic: Basket offerings: twelve kinds per chamber;

sentences.zh: 豆之實，每室十有二品。

translations.literal: the contents of the stem stands: twelve kinds per chamber.
translations.idiomatic: stem-stand offerings: twelve kinds per chamber.

sentences.zh: 凡祀，先期命貴臣率獵師取鮮獐鹿兔，以供脯臡醓醢。

translations.literal: For all sacrifices, beforehand a noble minister was ordered to lead huntsmen to take fresh roe deer and hare to supply dried meat, minced meat, pickled meat, and sauces.
translations.idiomatic: Before each sacrifice a noble minister led huntsmen to take fresh roe deer and hare for dried meat, minced meat, pickles, and sauces.

sentences.zh: 稻粱為飯，每室二簠；

translations.literal: Rice and millet as cooked grain: two square baskets per chamber;
translations.idiomatic: Rice and millet as cooked grain: two square baskets per chamber;

sentences.zh: 黍稷為飯，每室二簋。

translations.literal: panicled millet and glutinous millet as cooked grain: two round baskets per chamber.
translations.idiomatic: panicled and glutinous millet as cooked grain: two round baskets per chamber.

sentences.zh: 彜尊之實，每室十有一。

translations.literal: The contents of the ritual wine vessels: eleven per chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual wine vessels: eleven kinds per chamber.

sentences.zh: 明水玄酒，用陰鑒取水於月，與井水同，鬯用郁金為之。

translations.literal: Clear water and dark wine: clear water was drawn with a yin mirror from the moon, together with well water; spiced libation wine was made from turmeric.
translations.idiomatic: Clear water and dark wine: clear water was drawn at moonrise with a yin mirror, together with well water; spiced libation wine was made from turmeric.

sentences.zh: 五齊三酒，醞於光祿寺。

translations.literal: The five clarified wines and three wines were brewed at the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: The five clarified wines and three wines were brewed at the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 膟膋蕭蒿，至元十八年五月弗用，後遂廢。

translations.literal: Fatty meat, minced flesh, mugwort, and wormwood were discontinued in the fifth month of the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan and were later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Fatty meat, minced flesh, mugwort, and wormwood were dropped in the fifth month of Zhiyuan 18 and later abolished altogether.

sentences.zh: 茅香以縮酒，至元十七年，始用沅州麻陽縣包茅。

translations.literal: Thatch grass was used to filter wine; in the seventeenth year of Zhiyuan, thatch from Baomao in Yuanzhou was first used.
translations.idiomatic: Thatch grass filtered the wine; from Zhiyuan 17 thatch from Baomao in Yuanzhou was used.

sentences.zh: 天鵝、野馬、塔剌不花、

translations.literal: Swans, wild horses, tarabghua,
translations.idiomatic: Swans, wild horses, tarabghua,

sentences.zh: （其狀如獾。）〉

translations.literal: (Its form resembles a badger.)
translations.idiomatic: (Its form resembles a badger.)

sentences.zh: 野雞、鸧、黃羊、胡寨兒、

translations.literal: pheasants, bustards, yellow sheep, husai'er,
translations.idiomatic: pheasants, bustards, yellow sheep, husai'er,

sentences.zh: （其狀如鳩。）〉

translations.literal: (Its form resembles a dove.)
translations.idiomatic: (Its form resembles a dove.)

sentences.zh: 湩乳、葡萄酒，以國禮割奠，皆列室用之。

translations.literal: koumiss and grape wine—for the national rite of cutting and presentation—all were used and set out in the row of chambers.
translations.idiomatic: koumiss and grape wine, presented in the national cutting-and-presentation rite, were set out in each chamber.

sentences.zh: 羊一，豕一，籩之實二栗、鹿脯，豆之實二菁菹、鹿臡，簠之實黍，簋之實稷，爵尊之實酒，皆七祀位各用之。

translations.literal: One sheep, one swine, two kinds in the basket stands—chestnuts and dried venison; two kinds in the stem stands—pickled greens and minced venison; panicled millet in the square basket, glutinous millet in the round basket, and wine in the goblet and ritual vessels—all were used, each at its own seat for the seven sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: For the seven sacrifices each seat received one sheep and one swine; basket stands held chestnuts and dried venison, stem stands pickled greens and minced venison, square baskets panicled millet, round baskets glutinous millet, and goblets and ritual vessels wine.

sentences.zh: 薦新鮪、野彘，孟春用之。

translations.literal: Fresh tuna and wild boar were offered as seasonal gifts, used in the first month of spring.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh tuna and wild boar were seasonal offerings for the first month of spring.

sentences.zh: 雁、天鵝，仲春用之。

translations.literal: Wild geese and swans were used in the second month of spring.
translations.idiomatic: Wild geese and swans were offered in the second month of spring.

sentences.zh: 葑韭、鴨雞卵，季春用之。

translations.literal: Water-shield, leeks, and duck eggs were used in the last month of spring.
translations.idiomatic: Water-shield, leeks, and duck eggs were seasonal offerings for the last month of spring.

sentences.zh: 冰、羔羊，孟夏用之。

translations.literal: Ice and lamb kids were used in the first month of summer.
translations.idiomatic: Ice and lamb kids were offered in the first month of summer.

sentences.zh: 櫻桃、竹筍、蒲筍、羊，仲夏用之。

translations.literal: Cherries, bamboo shoots, cattail shoots, and sheep were used in the second month of summer.
translations.idiomatic: Cherries, bamboo shoots, cattail shoots, and sheep were seasonal offerings for the second month of summer.

sentences.zh: 瓜、豚、大麥飯、小麥面，季夏用之。

translations.literal: Melons, suckling pigs, barley rice, and wheat flour were used in the last month of summer.
translations.idiomatic: Melons, suckling pigs, barley rice, and wheat flour were offered in the last month of summer.

sentences.zh: 雛雞，孟秋用之。

translations.literal: Chicks were used in the first month of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Chicks were seasonal offerings for the first month of autumn.

sentences.zh: 菱芡、栗、黃鼠，仲秋用之。

translations.literal: Water caltrop, foxnut, chestnuts, and yellow rats were used in the second month of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Water caltrop, foxnut, chestnuts, and yellow rats were offered in the second month of autumn.

sentences.zh: 梨、棗、黍、粱、鶿老，季秋用之。

translations.literal: Pears, jujubes, panicled millet, glutinous millet, and cormorants were used in the last month of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Pears, jujubes, panicled millet, glutinous millet, and cormorants were seasonal offerings for the last month of autumn.

sentences.zh: 芝麻、兔、鹿、稻米飯，孟冬用之。

translations.literal: Sesame, rabbits, deer, and rice meals were used in the first month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: Sesame, rabbits, deer, and rice meals were offered in the first month of winter.

sentences.zh: 麕、野馬，仲冬用之。

translations.literal: River deer and wild horses were used in the second month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: River deer and wild horses were seasonal offerings for the second month of winter.

sentences.zh: 鯉、黃羊、塔剌不花，季冬用之。

translations.literal: Carp, yellow sheep, and tarabghua were used in the last month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: Carp, yellow sheep, and tarabghua were offered in the last month of winter.

sentences.zh: 至大元年春正月，皇太子言薦新增用影堂品物，羊羔、炙魚、饅頭、饣其子、西域湯餅、圜米粥、砂糖飯羹，每月用以配薦。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the first year of Zhida, the crown prince proposed that seasonal offerings newly add shadow-hall items: lamb kids, broiled fish, steamed buns, glutinous rice cakes, Western Region soup noodles, round rice porridge, and sugar-sweetened rice broth—each month to be paired in presentation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of Zhida 1, the crown prince urged that the seasonal offerings add shadow-hall fare: lamb kids, broiled fish, steamed buns, glutinous rice cakes, Western Region soup noodles, round rice porridge, and sugar-sweetened rice broth, presented each month as paired offerings.

sentences.zh: 祭器：籩十有二，冪以青巾，巾繪彩雲。

translations.literal: Sacrificial vessels: twelve basket stands, veiled with green cloth painted with colored clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial vessels: twelve basket stands, each veiled with green cloth painted with colored clouds.

sentences.zh: 豆十有四，一實毛血，一實膟膋。

translations.literal: Fourteen stem stands, one filled with raw blood and hair, one with fatty meat and minced flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen stem stands—one holding raw blood and hair, one fatty meat and minced flesh.

sentences.zh: 登三，铏三，有柶。

translations.literal: Three elevated vessels, three tripods, with ladles.
translations.idiomatic: Three elevated vessels and three tripods, each with ladles.

sentences.zh: 簠二，簋二，有匕箸。

translations.literal: Two square baskets, two round baskets, with spoons and chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Two square baskets and two round baskets, with spoons and chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 俎七，以載牲體，皆有鼎。

translations.literal: Seven offering tables, to bear the sacrificial flesh, each with a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Seven offering tables to bear the sacrificial flesh, each paired with a cauldron.

sentences.zh: 後以盤貯牲體，盤置俎上，鼎不用。

translations.literal: Later trays stored the sacrificial flesh, trays placed upon the offering tables; cauldrons were not used.
translations.idiomatic: Later, trays held the sacrificial flesh on the offering tables, and cauldrons were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 香案一。

translations.literal: One incense table.
translations.idiomatic: One incense table.

sentences.zh: 銷金絳羅衣。

translations.literal: Gilded crimson silk vestments.
translations.idiomatic: Gilded crimson silk vestments.

sentences.zh: 銀香鼎一，銀香奩一，茅苴盤一，實以沙。

translations.literal: One silver incense censer, one silver incense box, one thatch-grass tray filled with sand.
translations.idiomatic: One silver incense censer, one silver incense box, and one thatch-grass tray filled with sand.

sentences.zh: 已上並陳室內。

translations.literal: All the above were set out within the chambers.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above were arranged inside the chambers.

sentences.zh: 燎爐一，實以炭。

translations.literal: One brazier, filled with charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: One brazier filled with charcoal.

sentences.zh: 篚一，實以蕭蒿黍稷。

translations.literal: One hamper, filled with mugwort, wormwood, panicled millet, and glutinous millet.
translations.idiomatic: One hamper holding mugwort, wormwood, panicled millet, and glutinous millet.

sentences.zh: 祝案一，紫羅衣，置祝文於上，銷金絳羅覆之。

translations.literal: One prayer table with purple silk vestments; the prayer text was placed upon it and covered with gilded crimson silk.
translations.idiomatic: One prayer table draped in purple silk; the prayer text lay upon it beneath a gilded crimson silk cover.

sentences.zh: 雞彜一，有舟；

translations.literal: One rooster yi, with base;
translations.idiomatic: One rooster yi, with base;

sentences.zh: 鳥彜一，有舟，加勺；

translations.literal: one bird yi, with base and ladle;
translations.idiomatic: one bird yi, with base and ladle;

sentences.zh: 春夏用之。

translations.literal: used in spring and summer.
translations.idiomatic: used in spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 斝彜一，有舟；

translations.literal: One jia yi, with base;
translations.idiomatic: One jia yi, with base;

sentences.zh: 黃彜一，有舟，加勺；

translations.literal: one yellow yi, with base and ladle;
translations.idiomatic: one yellow yi, with base and ladle;

sentences.zh: 秋冬用之。

translations.literal: used in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: used in autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 虎彜一，有舟；

translations.literal: One tiger yi, with base;
translations.idiomatic: One tiger yi, with base;

sentences.zh: 蜼彜一，有舟，加勺；

translations.literal: one wei yi, with base and ladle;
translations.idiomatic: one wei yi, with base and ladle;

sentences.zh: 特祭用之。

translations.literal: used for special sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: used for special sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 凡雞彜、斝彜、虎彜以實明水，鳥彜、黃彜、蜼彜以實鬯。

translations.literal: In general the rooster yi, jia yi, and tiger yi held clear water; the bird yi, yellow yi, and wei yi held spiced libation wine.
translations.idiomatic: The rooster, jia, and tiger yi held clear water; the bird, yellow, and wei yi held spiced libation wine.

sentences.zh: 犧尊二，象尊二，春夏用之。

translations.literal: Two sacrificial-ox vessels and two elephant vessels, used in spring and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Two sacrificial-ox vessels and two elephant vessels for spring and summer.

sentences.zh: 著尊二，壺尊二，秋冬用之。

translations.literal: Two zhu vessels and two hu vessels, used in autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: Two zhu vessels and two hu vessels for autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 太尊二，山尊二，特祭用之。

translations.literal: Two tai vessels and two mountain vessels, used for special sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Two tai vessels and two mountain vessels for special sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尊皆有坫勺，冪以白布巾，巾繪黼文。

translations.literal: All vessels had stands and ladles; veils were of white cloth painted with fu patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Every vessel had a stand and ladle; white cloth veils were painted with fu patterns.

sentences.zh: 著尊二，山罍二，皆有坫加冪。

translations.literal: Two zhu vessels and two mountain jars, all with stands and veils.
translations.idiomatic: Two zhu vessels and two mountain jars, each with stand and veil.

sentences.zh: 已上並陳室外。

translations.literal: All the above were set out outside the chambers.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above were arranged outside the chambers.

sentences.zh: 壺尊二，太尊二，山罍四，皆有坫加冪，藉以莞席，並陳殿下，北向西上，設而不酌，每室皆同。

translations.literal: Two hu vessels, two tai vessels, four mountain jars—all with stands and veils, spread on rush mats, all set beneath the hall facing north and ranked west to east, established but not poured; each chamber was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Two hu vessels, two tai vessels, and four mountain jars, each with stand and veil on rush mats, were set beneath the hall facing north, ranked west to east, filled but not poured—identically in every chamber.

sentences.zh: 通廊禦香案一，銷金黃羅衣，銀香奩一，貯禦祝香，銷金帕覆之，並陳殿中央。

translations.literal: In the connecting corridor one imperial incense table with gilded yellow silk vestments, one silver incense box storing imperial prayer incense covered with gilded silk, all set at the center of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the connecting corridor stood one imperial incense table in gilded yellow silk, one silver incense box of imperial prayer incense beneath a gilded silk cover—all at the center of the hall.

sentences.zh: 罍洗所罍二，洗二，一以供爵滌，一以供盥潔。

translations.literal: At the jar-washing station two jars and two basins, one to rinse goblets, one for hand-washing.
translations.idiomatic: At the jar-washing station were two jars and two basins—one for rinsing goblets, one for ablutions.

sentences.zh: 篚二，實以璋瓚巾、塗金銀爵。

translations.literal: Two hampers, filled with jade scepter cloths and gilded silver goblets.
translations.idiomatic: Two hampers holding jade-scepter cloths and gilded silver goblets.

sentences.zh: 七祀神位，籩二，豆二，簠一，簋一，俎一，爵一有坫，香案一，沙池一，壺尊二有坫加冪，七祀皆同。

translations.literal: For the seven sacrifices spirit seats: two basket stands, two stem stands, one square basket, one round basket, one offering table, one goblet with stand, one incense table, one sand pool, two hu vessels with stands and veils—the seven sacrifices were all alike.
translations.idiomatic: At each of the seven sacrifices: two basket stands, two stem stands, one square basket, one round basket, one offering table, one goblet on its stand, one incense table, one sand pool, and two hu vessels with stands and veils—all seven were identical.

sentences.zh: 罍一、洗一、篚一，中統以來，雜金、宋祭器而用之。

translations.literal: One jar, one basin, one hamper—from the Zhongtong era onward, mixed gold and Song sacrificial vessels were used.
translations.idiomatic: One jar, one basin, and one hamper; from the Zhongtong era onward gold and Song sacrificial vessels were used interchangeably.

sentences.zh: 至治初，始造新器於江浙行省，其舊器悉置幾閣。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhizhi era, new vessels were first cast in the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat; the old vessels were all placed in side cabinets.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhizhi era new vessels were first cast in the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and the old ones were stored in side cabinets.

sentences.zh: 親祀時享儀，其目有八：

translations.literal: The protocol for the emperor personally performing seasonal offerings had eight headings:
translations.idiomatic: The protocol for the emperor personally performing seasonal temple offerings comprised eight sections:

sentences.zh: 一曰齋戒。

translations.literal: First, abstention.
translations.idiomatic: First: abstention.

sentences.zh: 前祀七日，皇帝散齋四日於別殿，治事如故，不作樂，停奏刑名事，不行刑罰。

translations.literal: Seven days before the sacrifice, the emperor observed four days of preliminary abstention in a separate hall, conducting affairs as usual but without music, suspending reports of criminal cases, and imposing no punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days before the rite the emperor spent four days in preliminary abstention in a separate hall, still conducting affairs but without music, criminal reports, or punishments.

sentences.zh: 致齋三日，惟專心祀事，其二日於大明殿，一日於大次。

translations.literal: Three days of strict abstention were devoted solely to the sacrifice: two days in the Hall of Great Brightness, one day in the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: Three days of strict abstention were devoted solely to the sacrifice—two in the Hall of Great Brightness, one in the great tent.

sentences.zh: 致齋前一日，尚舍監設禦幄於大明殿西序，東向。

translations.literal: On the day before strict abstention, the Director of the Imperial Household set the imperial curtain at the western wing of the Hall of Great Brightness, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of strict abstention the Director of the Imperial Household hung the imperial curtain in the western wing of the Hall of Great Brightness, facing east.

sentences.zh: 致齋之日質明，諸衛勒所部屯列。

translations.literal: At dawn on the day of strict abstention, the guards of each command arrayed their units.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the day of strict abstention each guard command arrayed its troops.

sentences.zh: 晝漏下一刻，通事舍人引侍享執事文武四品以上官，俱公服詣別殿奉迎。

translations.literal: At the first quarter of the day clepsydra, the Herald of Affairs led civil and military officers of the fourth rank and above who were to attend the offering, all in court dress, to the separate hall to welcome the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the first quarter after dawn the Herald of Affairs led attending civil and military officers of the fourth rank and above, in court dress, to the separate hall to welcome the emperor.

sentences.zh: 二刻，侍中版奏請中嚴，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍。

translations.literal: At the second quarter, the attendant grandee reported by placard requesting the inner vigil; the emperor donned the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: At the second quarter the attendant grandee reported by placard for the inner vigil; the emperor donned the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 三刻，侍中版奏外辦，皇帝結佩出別殿，乘輿，華蓋傘扇侍衛如常儀，奉引至大明殿禦幄，東向坐，侍臣夾侍如常。

translations.literal: At the third quarter, the attendant grandee reported by placard that outer preparations were complete; the emperor fastened his girdle, left the separate hall, mounted the palanquin, and with canopy, parasol, and fan escort as in the usual protocol was conducted to the imperial curtain in the Hall of Great Brightness, where he sat facing east with attendants flanking him as usual.
translations.idiomatic: At the third quarter the attendant grandee reported outer preparations complete; the emperor secured his girdle, left the separate hall, mounted the palanquin, and with the usual canopy and escort was led to the imperial curtain in the Hall of Great Brightness, where he sat facing east with attendants at his sides.

sentences.zh: 一刻頃，侍中前跪奏言請降就齋，俯伏興。

translations.literal: After about one quarter, the attendant grandee advanced, knelt, and reported requesting that he descend to enter abstention, then prostrated himself and rose.
translations.idiomatic: After about one quarter the attendant grandee knelt and asked that the emperor descend to enter abstention, then prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降座入室，侍享執事官各還所司，宿衛者如常。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from his seat and entered the chamber; the attending officers each returned to their offices, and the night guards remained as usual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left his seat and entered the abstention chamber; attending officers returned to their offices while night guards stood as usual.

sentences.zh: 凡應祀官受誓戒於中書省。

translations.literal: All officers who were to take part in the sacrifice received sworn injunctions at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: All officers due to sacrifice received sworn injunctions at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 散齋四日，致齋三日。

translations.literal: Preliminary abstention four days, strict abstention three days.
translations.idiomatic: Four days of preliminary abstention, three of strict abstention.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿鑒取明水、火。

translations.literal: The Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments drew clear water and fire by mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments drew clear water and fire by mirror.

sentences.zh: 火以供爨，水以實尊。

translations.literal: Fire was for cooking; water was to fill the vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Fire served cooking; water filled the ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 二曰陳設。

translations.literal: Second, arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Second: arrangement.

sentences.zh: 祀前三日，尚舍監陳大次於西神門外道北，南向。

translations.literal: Three days before the sacrifice, the Director of the Imperial Household set out the great tent north of the road outside the Western Spirit Gate, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before the rite the Director of the Imperial Household erected the great tent north of the road outside the Western Spirit Gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 設小次於西階西，東向。

translations.literal: The small tent was set west of the western steps, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The small tent stood west of the western steps, facing east.

sentences.zh: 設版位於西神門內，橫街南，東向。

translations.literal: The spirit tablet seat was set inside the Western Spirit Gate, south of the cross street, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit-tablet seat was placed inside the Western Spirit Gate, south of the cross street, facing east.

sentences.zh: 設飲福位於太室尊彜所，稍東，西向。

translations.literal: The blessing-drinking seat was set at the Grand Chamber ritual vessels, slightly east, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The blessing-drinking seat was placed by the Grand Chamber vessels, slightly to the east and facing west.

sentences.zh: 設黃道裀褥於大次前，至西神門，至小次版位西階及殿門之外。

translations.literal: Yellow-carpet cushions were laid from before the great tent to the Western Spirit Gate, to the western steps of the small tent and spirit tablet seat, and outside the hall doors.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow-carpet cushions ran from before the great tent to the Western Spirit Gate, the western steps of the small tent and tablet seat, and outside the hall doors.

sentences.zh: 設禦洗位於禦板位東，稍北，北向。

translations.literal: The imperial washing seat was set east of the imperial tablet seat, slightly north, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial washing seat lay east of the imperial tablet seat, slightly north and facing north.

sentences.zh: 設亞終獻位於西神門內禦板位稍南，東向。

translations.literal: The second and final presenters seats were set slightly south inside the Western Spirit Gate from the imperial tablet seat, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: Seats for the second and final presenters were placed slightly south of the imperial tablet seat inside the Western Spirit Gate, facing east.

sentences.zh: 以北為上，罍洗在其東北。

translations.literal: North was regarded as superior; the jar-washing station was to its northeast.
translations.idiomatic: North ranked highest; the jar-washing station stood to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 設亞終獻飲福位於禦飲福位後，稍南，西向。

translations.literal: The second and final presenters blessing-drinking seats were set behind the imperial blessing-drinking seat, slightly south, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing-drinking seats for the second and final presenters were behind the imperial seat, slightly south and facing west.

sentences.zh: 陳設八寶黃羅案於西階西，隨地之宜。

translations.literal: The eight treasures yellow-silk table was set west of the western steps, according to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The table for the eight treasures in yellow silk was placed west of the western steps as the terrain allowed.

sentences.zh: 設享官宮縣樂、省牲位、諸執事公卿御史位，並如常儀。

translations.literal: Seats for the offering officers palace music, the inspection of victims, and the attending grandees and censors were all as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Positions for palace music, victim inspection, and attending grandees and censors followed the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 殿上下及各室，設簠、簋、籩、豆、尊、罍、彜、斝等器，並如常儀。

translations.literal: Above and below the hall and in each chamber, square baskets, round baskets, basket stands, stem stands, vessels, jars, yi, and jia were all set as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall and every chamber, square and round baskets, basket and stem stands, vessels, jars, yi, and jia were arranged per the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 三曰車駕出宮。

translations.literal: Third, the imperial procession leaving the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the imperial procession leaving the palace.

sentences.zh: 祀前一日，所司備法駕鹵簿於崇天門外，太僕卿率其屬備玉輅於大明門外。

translations.literal: On the day before the sacrifice, the responsible offices prepared the statutory guard of honor outside the Gate of Ascending to Heaven; the Minister of the Imperial Stud led his subordinates to prepare the jade chariot outside the Gate of Great Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the rite the responsible offices prepared the statutory guard outside the Gate of Ascending to Heaven, and the Minister of the Imperial Stud prepared the jade chariot outside the Gate of Great Brightness.

sentences.zh: 千牛將軍執刀於輅前，北向。

translations.literal: The Thousand-Ox General held a blade before the chariot, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Thousand-Ox General stood with blade before the chariot, facing north.

sentences.zh: 其日質明，諸侍享執事官，先詣太廟祀所。

translations.literal: At dawn that day, all attending officers went first to the Imperial Ancestral Temple sacrifice site.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn that day all attending officers went first to the temple sacrifice site.

sentences.zh: 諸侍臣直衛及導駕官於致齋殿前，左右分班立。

translations.literal: Attending ministers, direct guards, and procession guides stood in divided ranks before the abstention hall.
translations.idiomatic: Attending ministers, direct guards, and procession guides stood in divided ranks before the abstention hall.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人引侍中跪奏請中嚴，俯伏興。

translations.literal: The Herald of Affairs led the attendant grandee to kneel and report by placard requesting the inner vigil; he prostrated himself and rose.
translations.idiomatic: The Herald of Affairs led the attendant grandee to kneel and report by placard for the inner vigil; he prostrated and rose.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍。

translations.literal: The emperor donned the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor donned the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 少頃，侍中版奏外辦，皇帝出齋室，即御座。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, the attendant grandee reported by placard that outer preparations were complete; the emperor left the abstention chamber and took the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, the attendant grandee reported outer preparations complete; the emperor left the abstention chamber and took the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 群臣起居訖，尚輦進輿，侍中奏請皇帝升輿。

translations.literal: When the ministers had finished their greetings, the Director of the Imperial Carriage advanced the palanquin; the attendant grandee reported requesting that the emperor mount the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: After the ministers had greeted him, the Director of the Imperial Carriage brought the palanquin; the attendant grandee asked that the emperor mount.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升輿，華蓋傘扇侍衛如常儀。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the palanquin; canopy, parasol, and fan escort were as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted the palanquin with the usual canopy and escort.

sentences.zh: 導駕官前導至大明門外，侍中進當輿前，跪奏請皇帝降輿升輅。

translations.literal: Procession guides led ahead to outside the Gate of Great Brightness; the attendant grandee advanced before the palanquin, knelt, and reported requesting that the emperor descend from the palanquin and mount the chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Procession guides led to the Gate of Great Brightness; the attendant grandee knelt before the palanquin and asked the emperor to descend and mount the chariot.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升輅，太僕執禦，導駕官分左右步導。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted the chariot; the Minister of the Imperial Stud held the reins; procession guides walked in divided ranks left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mounted the chariot; the Minister of the Imperial Stud held the reins while guides walked left and right.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎進當輅前，跪奏請車駕進發。

translations.literal: The vice minister of the Gate Department advanced before the chariot, knelt, and reported requesting that the procession depart.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister of the Gate Department knelt before the chariot and asked that the procession depart.

sentences.zh: 車駕動，稱警蹕。

translations.literal: The procession moved; the cry "Halt the way!" was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The procession moved; the cry to clear the way was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 千牛將軍夾而趨至崇天門外，門下侍郎跪奏請車駕少駐，敕眾官上馬。

translations.literal: The Thousand-Ox General flanked and hurried to outside the Gate of Ascending to Heaven; the vice minister of the Gate Department knelt and reported requesting that the procession pause briefly and command all officers to mount.
translations.idiomatic: The Thousand-Ox General flanked the chariot to the Gate of Ascending to Heaven; the vice minister knelt and asked a brief halt so all officers might mount.

sentences.zh: 侍中承旨退，稱曰「制可」。

translations.literal: The attendant grandee received the command and withdrew, proclaiming, "The command is approved."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant grandee received the order, withdrew, and proclaimed, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎退，傳制稱眾官上馬。

translations.literal: The vice minister of the Gate Department withdrew and transmitted the command that all officers mount.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister withdrew and transmitted the order for all officers to mount.

sentences.zh: 贊者承傳敕眾官上馬。

translations.literal: The herald transmitted the command that all officers mount.
translations.idiomatic: The herald relayed the command for all officers to mount.

sentences.zh: 上馬訖，門下侍郎奏請敕車右升，侍中前承制，退稱曰「制可」。

translations.literal: When mounting was finished, the vice minister of the Gate Department reported requesting command for the chariot-right to mount; the attendant grandee advanced to receive the command and withdrew, proclaiming, "The command is approved."
translations.idiomatic: When all had mounted, the vice minister asked leave for the chariot-right to mount; the attendant grandee received the order, withdrew, and proclaimed, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 千牛將軍升訖，門下侍郎奏請車駕進發。

translations.literal: When the Thousand-Ox General had mounted, the vice minister of the Gate Department reported requesting that the procession depart.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Thousand-Ox General had mounted, the vice minister asked that the procession depart.

sentences.zh: 車駕動，稱警蹕。

translations.literal: The procession moved; the cry "Halt the way!" was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The procession moved; again the cry to clear the way was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎奉八寶與殿中監部從在黃鉞內，教坊樂前引，鼓吹不振作。

translations.literal: The Keeper of Seals bore the eight treasures with the Director of the Palace Department following within the yellow halberd guard; Music Bureau players led ahead; drums and pipes were not sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The Keeper of Seals bore the eight treasures with the Director of the Palace Department inside the yellow-halberd guard; Music Bureau players led, but drums and pipes were silent.

sentences.zh: 將至太廟，禮直官引諸侍享執事官於廟門外，左右立班，奉迎駕至廟門，回輅南向。

translations.literal: As they were about to reach the Imperial Ancestral Temple, ritual officers led the attending officers outside the temple gate to stand in divided ranks left and right, welcoming the procession to the temple gate, where the chariot turned south.
translations.idiomatic: Near the Imperial Ancestral Temple, ritual officers led attending officers to ranks outside the gate to welcome the emperor; at the gate the chariot turned south.

sentences.zh: 將軍降立於輅左，侍中於輅前奏稱侍中臣某請皇帝降輅，步入廟門。

translations.literal: The general descended and stood to the left of the chariot; the attendant grandee before the chariot reported, "The attendant grandee, your subject So-and-so, requests that the emperor descend from the chariot and enter the temple gate on foot."
translations.idiomatic: The general descended to the left of the chariot; before the chariot the attendant grandee reported, "Your subject, attendant grandee So-and-so, requests that Your Majesty descend and enter the temple gate on foot."

sentences.zh: 皇帝降輅，導駕官前導，皇帝步入廟門稍西。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from the chariot; procession guides led ahead, and the emperor entered the temple gate slightly to the west.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended; guides led ahead as he entered the temple gate, slightly west.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏請皇帝升輿，尚輦奉輿，華蓋傘扇如常儀。

translations.literal: The attendant grandee reported requesting that the emperor mount the palanquin; the Director of the Imperial Carriage presented the palanquin; canopy, parasol, and fan escort were as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant grandee asked the emperor to mount the palanquin; the Director of the Imperial Carriage brought it forward, with the usual canopy and escort.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘輿至大次，侍中奏請皇帝降輿入就大次。

translations.literal: The emperor rode the palanquin to the great tent; the attendant grandee reported requesting that the emperor descend from the palanquin and enter and take his place in the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode the palanquin to the great tent; the attendant grandee asked him to descend and enter it.

sentences.zh: 皇帝入就次，簾降，宿衛如式，尚食進膳如儀。

translations.literal: The emperor entered and took his place; the curtain was lowered; night guards were as prescribed; the Director of Imperial Food Service brought meals as in the protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his place; the curtain lowered; night guards stood as prescribed while the Director of Imperial Food Service served meals per protocol.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使以祝版奏禦署訖，奉出，太廟令受之，各奠於坫，置各室祝案上。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner presented the prayer tablet by report for the imperial signature; when this was finished he bore it out; the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple received it and each tablet was set on its stand and placed on the prayer table of each chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner presented the prayer tablet for the emperor's signature; when done he carried it out, and the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple received it and set each tablet on its stand on the prayer table in each chamber.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人承旨，敕眾官各還齋次。

translations.literal: The Herald of Affairs received the command and ordered all officers each to return to their fasting quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Herald of Affairs received the order and directed all officers to return to their fasting quarters.

sentences.zh: 四曰省牲器。

translations.literal: Fourth, inspection of victims and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: inspection of victims and vessels.

sentences.zh: 祀前一日未後三刻，廩犧令丞、太官令丞、太祝以牲就位。

translations.literal: On the day before the sacrifice, at the third quarter after wei, the superintendents of grain and sacrificial animals, the superintendents of the grand food service, and the chief sacrifiers placed the victims in position.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the rite, at the third quarter after wei, the superintendents of sacrificial animals and food service and the chief sacrifiers positioned the victims.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常卿、光祿卿丞、監祭禮等官就位。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the Minister of Court Ceremonies, the director and assistant of palace delicacies, and the sacrifice supervisors and other officers to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the Minister of Court Ceremonies, the Director of Palace Delicacies and his assistant, the sacrifice supervisors, and other officers to their posts.

sentences.zh: 禮直官請太常、監祭、監禮由東神門北偏門入，升自東階。

translations.literal: Ritual officers requested that the Minister of Court Ceremonies, the sacrifice supervisor, and the ritual supervisor enter by the north side door of the Eastern Spirit Gate and ascend by the eastern steps.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers had the Minister of Court Ceremonies, the sacrifice supervisor, and the ritual supervisor enter through the north side door of the Eastern Spirit Gate and ascend the eastern steps.

sentences.zh: 每位視滌祭器，司尊彜舉冪曰「潔」。

translations.literal: At each seat they inspected the purification vessels; the Keeper of Vessels lifted the veil and said, "Clean."
translations.idiomatic: At each seat they inspected the purification vessels; the Keeper of Vessels raised the veil and called, "Clean."

sentences.zh: 俱畢，降自東階，由東神門北偏門出，復位，立定。

translations.literal: When all was finished they descended by the eastern steps, went out by the north side door of the Eastern Spirit Gate, returned to their posts, and stood in place.
translations.idiomatic: When finished they descended the eastern steps, left by the north side door of the Eastern Spirit Gate, returned to their posts, and stood in place.

sentences.zh: 禮直官稍前曰「請省牲」，引太常卿視牲，退復位。

translations.literal: A ritual officer stepped slightly forward and said, "Please inspect the victims," and led the Minister of Court Ceremonies to inspect the victims; he withdrew and returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: A ritual officer stepped forward and said, "Please inspect the victims," then led the Minister of Court Ceremonies to inspect them and return to his post.

sentences.zh: 次引廩犧令出班，巡牲一匝，西向折身曰「充」。

translations.literal: Next he led the superintendent of grain and sacrificial animals from the ranks; he circled the victims once, turned west, bowed, and said, "Sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Next he led the superintendent of sacrificial animals from the ranks to circle the victims once, turn west, bow, and say, "Sufficient."

sentences.zh: 諸太祝巡牲一匝，上一員出班西向折身曰「腯」畢，俱復位。

translations.literal: The chief sacrifiers circled the victims once; the senior one stepped from the ranks, turned west, bowed, and said, "Plump"; when finished, all returned to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The chief sacrifiers circled the victims once; the senior one stepped out, turned west, bowed, and said, "Plump," then all returned to their posts.

sentences.zh: 蒙古巫祝致詞訖，禮直官稍前曰「請詣省饌位」，引太常卿、光祿卿、監祭、監禮、光祿丞、大官令丞詣省饌位，東西相向立定，以北為上。

translations.literal: When the Mongol shaman had finished his invocation, a ritual officer stepped slightly forward and said, "Please proceed to the food-inspection post," and led the Minister of Court Ceremonies, the Director of Palace Delicacies, the sacrifice supervisor, the ritual supervisor, the assistant director of palace delicacies, and the superintendents of the grand food service to the food-inspection post, where they stood facing east and west, with north regarded as superior.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mongol shaman had finished his invocation, a ritual officer said, "Please proceed to inspect the offerings," and led the Minister of Court Ceremonies, the Director of Palace Delicacies, the sacrifice and ritual supervisors, the assistant director, and the food-service superintendents to the inspection post, where they stood facing each other with north as the superior side.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常卿詣饌殿內省饌。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the Minister of Court Ceremonies into the offering hall to inspect the offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the Minister of Court Ceremonies into the offering hall to inspect the food.

sentences.zh: 視饌訖，禮直官引太常卿還齋所。

translations.literal: When the inspection of offerings was finished, ritual officers led the Minister of Court Ceremonies back to the fasting lodge.
translations.idiomatic: When the inspection was finished, ritual officers led the Minister of Court Ceremonies back to the fasting lodge.

sentences.zh: 次引廩犧令丞、諸太祝以次牽牲詣廚，授太官令。

translations.literal: Next ritual officers led the superintendents of grain and sacrificial animals and the chief sacrifiers in order to lead the victims to the kitchen and hand them over to the Director of the Grand Food Service.
translations.idiomatic: Next ritual officers led the superintendents of sacrificial animals and the chief sacrifiers, in order, to bring the victims to the kitchen and deliver them to the Director of the Grand Food Service.

sentences.zh: 次引光祿卿丞、監祭、監禮詣廚省鼎鑊，視滌溉訖，各還齋所。

translations.literal: Next ritual officers led the director and assistant of palace delicacies, the sacrifice supervisor, and the ritual supervisor to the kitchen to inspect the cauldrons and washing; when finished, each returned to the fasting lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Next they led the Director of Palace Delicacies and his assistant, the sacrifice supervisor, and the ritual supervisor to inspect the cauldrons and washing in the kitchen, then each returned to the fasting lodge.

sentences.zh: 太官令帥宰人以鸞刀割牲，祝史各取毛血，每位共實一豆，以肝洗於郁鬯及取膟膋，每位共實一豆，置於各位。

translations.literal: The Director of the Grand Food Service led the butchers to cut the victims with the phoenix knife; each prayer officer took hair and blood, one stem-stand for each seat in all; the liver was washed in scented libation liquor and the omentum was taken, one stem-stand for each seat in all, and set at each post.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Grand Food Service led butchers to cut the victims with the phoenix knife; prayer officers collected hair and blood into one stem-stand per seat, washed the liver in scented libation liquor and took the omentum into another stem-stand per seat, and set them at each post.

sentences.zh: 饌室內，庖人烹牲。

translations.literal: Within the offering hall, cooks cooked the victims.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the offering hall, cooks prepared the victims.

sentences.zh: 五曰晨稞。

translations.literal: Fifth, morning libation.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: morning libation.

sentences.zh: 祀日醜前五刻，諸享陪位官各服其服。

translations.literal: At the fifth quarter before chou on the day of the sacrifice, all officers attending the offering and sharing the seats donned their prescribed garments.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth quarter before chou on the day of the rite, all attending and co-offering officers put on their prescribed garments.

sentences.zh: 光祿卿、良醞令、太官令入，實籩、豆、簠、簋、尊、罍，各如常儀。

translations.literal: The Director of Palace Delicacies, the Director of Fine Brew, and the Director of the Grand Food Service entered and filled the basket stands, stem stands, square baskets, round baskets, vessels, and jars, each as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Palace Delicacies, the Director of Fine Brew, and the Director of the Grand Food Service entered and filled basket stands, stem stands, square and round baskets, vessels, and jars per the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 太樂令率工人二舞，以次入。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Music Office led the two dance troupes of workers to enter in order.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Music Office led the two dance companies of workers to enter in order.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎贊者先入就位，禮直官引御史、博士及執事者以次各入，就位，並如常儀。

translations.literal: The ceremonial attendants and heralds entered first and took their posts; ritual officers led the censor, erudites, and attendants in order each to enter and take their posts, all as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial attendants and heralds entered first and took their posts; ritual officers then led censors, erudites, and attendants in to their posts, all per the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒以下官升殿，分香設酒，如常儀。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the Minister of Education and officers below him up the hall to distribute incense and set out wine, as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the Minister of Education and officers below him up the hall to distribute incense and set out wine per the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常官、御史、博士升殿，視陳設，就位。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the Court of Ceremonies officers, censors, and erudites up the hall to inspect the arrangements and take their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led Court of Ceremonies officers, censors, and erudites up the hall to inspect the arrangements and take their posts.

sentences.zh: 復與太廟令、太祝、宮闈令升殿。

translations.literal: They again ascended the hall with the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the chief sacrifiers, and the Director of the Palace Gates.
translations.idiomatic: They again ascended with the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the chief sacrifiers, and the Director of the Palace Gates.

sentences.zh: 太祝出帝主，宮闈令出後主訖，御史及以上升殿官於當陛近西，北向立。

translations.literal: The chief sacrifiers brought out the emperor's spirit tablet; when the Director of the Palace Gates had brought out the empress's tablet, censors and all officers who had ascended the hall stood near the western side of the imperial steps, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The chief sacrifiers brought out the emperor's spirit tablet; when the Director of the Palace Gates had brought out the empress's tablet, censors and all officers on the hall stood near the west of the imperial steps, facing north.

sentences.zh: 奉禮於殿上贊奉神主訖，奉禮曰「再拜」，贊者承傳，諸官及執事者皆再拜，各就位。

translations.literal: On the hall the ceremonial attendant heralded that the spirit tablets had been presented; the ceremonial attendant said, "Bow twice"; the herald transmitted this, and all officers and attendants bowed twice and each returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall a ceremonial attendant announced the presentation of the spirit tablets and called, "Bow twice"; the herald relayed this, and all officers and attendants bowed twice and returned to their posts.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引亞終獻等官，由南神門東偏門入，就位，立定。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the second and final presenters and other officers to enter by the east side door of the Southern Spirit Gate and take their posts, standing in place.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the second and final presenters and other officers in through the east side door of the Southern Spirit Gate to their posts.

sentences.zh: 禮直官贊有司謹具，請行事。

translations.literal: A ritual officer heralded, "The responsible offices have carefully prepared; please proceed with the rite."
translations.idiomatic: A ritual officer announced, "The responsible offices have made all ready; please proceed with the rite."

sentences.zh: 協律郎俯伏興，舉麾，工鼓，宮縣樂作《思成之曲》，以黃鐘為宮，大呂為角，太簇為徵，應鐘為羽，作文舞九成止。

translations.literal: The pitch regulator prostrated himself and rose, raised the baton, the musicians drummed, palace music performed the piece "Thought Accomplished," with yellow bell as gong, great bell as jue, great cluster as zhi, and responding bell as yu, and the civil dance in nine sections ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The pitch regulator prostrated and rose, raised his baton, the musicians drummed, and palace music performed "Thought Accomplished" with yellow bell as gong, great bell as jue, great cluster as zhi, and responding bell as yu, ending with civil dance in nine sections.

sentences.zh: 樂奏將終，通事舍人引侍中版奏請中嚴。

translations.literal: As the music was about to end, the Herald of Affairs led the attendant grandee to report by placard requesting the inner vigil.
translations.idiomatic: As the music neared its end, the Herald of Affairs led the attendant grandee to report by placard for the inner vigil.

sentences.zh: 皇帝服袞冕，坐少頃，禮直官引博士，博士引禮儀使，對立於大次門外，當門北向。

translations.literal: The emperor donned the ceremonial crown and robe and sat briefly; ritual officers led the erudite, and the erudite led the ritual commissioner, to stand facing each other outside the great tent gate, facing north at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor donned his ceremonial crown and robe and sat briefly; ritual officers led an erudite, who led the ritual commissioner, to stand facing each other outside the great-tent gate, north-facing at the gate.

sentences.zh: 侍中奏外辦，禮儀使跪奏請皇帝行禮，俯伏興，簾卷。

translations.literal: The attendant grandee reported that outer preparations were complete; the ritual commissioner knelt and reported requesting that the emperor proceed with the rite, then prostrated himself and rose, and the curtain was rolled up.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant grandee reported outer preparations complete; the ritual commissioner knelt and asked the emperor to proceed with the rite, then prostrated and rose as the curtain rolled up.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎奉寶陳於西陛之西黃羅案上。

translations.literal: The Keeper of Seals bore the imperial seal and set it on the yellow-silk table west of the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: The Keeper of Seals bore the imperial seal and set it on the yellow-silk table west of the western steps.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出大次，博士、禮儀使前導，華蓋傘扇如儀，大禮使後從。

translations.literal: The emperor left the great tent; the erudite and ritual commissioner led ahead; canopy, parasol, and fan escort were as in the protocol; the grand ritual commissioner followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left the great tent; an erudite and the ritual commissioner led ahead with the prescribed canopy and escort, and the grand ritual commissioner followed.

sentences.zh: 至西神門外，殿中監跪進鎮圭，皇帝執圭，華蓋傘扇停於門外，近侍從入門。

translations.literal: At the outside of the Western Spirit Gate, the Director of the Palace Department knelt and advanced the tablet scepter; the emperor took the scepter; canopy, parasol, and fan escort halted outside the gate, and close attendants followed him in.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Western Spirit Gate the Director of the Palace Department knelt and presented the tablet scepter; the emperor took it while canopy and escort halted at the gate and close attendants followed him in.

sentences.zh: 協律郎跪俯伏興，舉麾，工鼓，宮縣《順成之樂》作。

translations.literal: The pitch regulator knelt, prostrated himself, and rose, raised the baton, the musicians drummed, and palace music performed "Accomplishment Attained."
translations.idiomatic: The pitch regulator knelt, prostrated and rose, raised his baton, the musicians drummed, and palace music performed "Accomplishment Attained."

sentences.zh: 至版位東向，協律郎偃麾，工戛，樂止。

translations.literal: When he reached the spirit-tablet seat facing east, the pitch regulator lowered the baton, the musicians ceased, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the spirit-tablet seat facing east the pitch regulator lowered his baton, the musicians stopped, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 引禮官分左右侍立，禮儀使前奏請再拜，皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: Guiding ritual officers stood left and right in attendance; the ritual commissioner advanced and reported requesting another bow; the emperor bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Guiding ritual officers stood to left and right; the ritual commissioner advanced and asked the emperor to bow again, and the emperor bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰「眾官再拜」，贊者承傳，凡在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The ceremonial attendant said, "All officers bow twice"; the herald transmitted this, and all who were in post bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: A ceremonial attendant called, "All officers bow twice"; the herald relayed this, and everyone in post bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇帝詣盥洗位，宮縣樂作，至洗位，樂止。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor proceed to the hand-washing post; palace music began; when he reached the washing post, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to proceed to the hand-washing post; palace music began and ceased when he arrived.

sentences.zh: 內侍跪取匜，興，沃水。

translations.literal: A palace attendant knelt, took the pouring vessel, rose, and poured water.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant knelt, took the pouring vessel, rose, and poured water.

sentences.zh: 又內侍跪取盤，興，承水。

translations.literal: Another palace attendant knelt, took the basin, rose, and received the water.
