translations.idiomatic: Another palace attendant knelt, took the basin, rose, and caught the water.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請搢鎮圭，皇帝搢圭，盥手訖，內侍跪取巾於篚，興，以進，帨手訖，皇帝詣爵洗位，奉瓚官以瓚跪進，皇帝受瓚，內侍奉匜沃水。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor insert the tablet scepter; the emperor inserted the scepter; when hand-washing was finished, a palace attendant knelt, took a cloth from the hamper, rose, and presented it; when drying the hands was finished, the emperor proceeded to the goblet-washing post; the officer bearing the libation vessel knelt and advanced the vessel; the emperor received the vessel; a palace attendant bore the pouring vessel and poured water.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to set aside the tablet scepter; the emperor did so, washed his hands, and dried them on a cloth from a hamper; he then went to the goblet-washing post, where the officer bearing the libation vessel knelt and presented it and a palace attendant poured water.

sentences.zh: 又內侍跪，奉盤承水，洗瓚訖，內侍奉巾以進，皇帝拭瓚訖，內侍奠盤匜，又奠巾於篚，奉瓚官跪受瓚。

translations.literal: Another palace attendant knelt, bore the basin to receive the water; when washing the vessel was finished, a palace attendant presented the cloth; when wiping the vessel was finished, the palace attendant set down the basin and pouring vessel, again set the cloth in the hamper, and the officer bearing the libation vessel knelt and received the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Another attendant caught the rinse water; when the vessel was washed and wiped, attendants set down basin and pouring vessel, returned the cloth to the hamper, and the officer bearing the libation vessel knelt to receive it back.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執鎮圭，前導皇帝升殿，宮縣樂作，至西階下，樂止。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take up the tablet scepter; he led the emperor ahead up the hall; palace music began; when they reached the foot of the western steps, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take up the tablet scepter and led him up the hall; palace music played until they reached the foot of the western steps.

sentences.zh: 皇帝升自西階，登歌樂作，禮儀使前導皇帝詣太祖室尊彜所，東向立，樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended by the western steps; ascent music began; the ritual commissioner led the emperor ahead to the ritual vessels of the Taizu chamber, where he stood facing east, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the western steps to ascent music; the ritual commissioner led him to the Taizu chamber vessels, where he stood facing east as the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 奉瓚官以瓚蒞鬯，司尊者舉冪，侍中跪酌郁鬯訖，禮儀使前導，入詣太祖神座前，北向立。

translations.literal: The officer bearing the libation vessel brought scented libation liquor; the Keeper of Vessels lifted the veil; the attendant grandee knelt and poured the scented libation liquor; when finished, the ritual commissioner led ahead and entered to the spirit seat of Taizu, standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The officer bearing the libation vessel brought scented liquor; the Keeper of Vessels raised the veil; the attendant grandee knelt and poured it; then the ritual commissioner led the emperor to Taizu's spirit seat, facing north.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請搢鎮圭跪，奉瓚官西向立，以瓚跪進。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor insert the tablet scepter and kneel; the officer bearing the libation vessel stood facing west and knelt to advance the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to set aside the tablet scepter and kneel; the officer bearing the libation vessel stood west-facing and knelt to present it.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執瓚、以鬯祼地，皇帝執瓚以鬯祼地，以瓚授奉瓚官。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take the vessel and pour the libation on the ground; the emperor took the vessel and poured the libation on the ground, then handed the vessel to the officer bearing the libation vessel.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take the vessel and pour libation on the ground; the emperor did so and returned the vessel to its bearer.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執鎮圭、俯伏興。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take up the tablet scepter and prostrate himself and rise.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take up the tablet scepter and prostrate and rise.

sentences.zh: 皇帝俯伏興，禮儀使前導出戶外褥位。

translations.literal: The emperor prostrated himself and rose; the ritual commissioner led ahead to the cushion outside the door.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prostrated and rose; the ritual commissioner led him to the cushion outside the door.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請再拜。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting another bow.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked for another bow.

sentences.zh: 皇帝再拜訖，禮儀使前導詣第二室以下，祼鬯並如上儀。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished bowing twice, the ritual commissioner led ahead to the second chamber and below; pouring libation liquor was all as in the protocol above.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor bowed twice, the ritual commissioner led him to the second chamber and those below, performing ground libation by the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 祼訖，禮儀使奏請還版位。

translations.literal: When the libation was finished, the ritual commissioner reported requesting that he return to the spirit-tablet seat.
translations.idiomatic: When libation was finished, the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to return to the spirit-tablet seat.

sentences.zh: 登歌樂作，皇帝降自西階，樂止。

translations.literal: Ascent music began; the emperor descended by the western steps, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music began as the emperor descended the western steps, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 宮縣樂作，至版位東向立，樂止。

translations.literal: Palace music began; he reached the spirit-tablet seat and stood facing east, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Palace music played as he reached the spirit-tablet seat and stood facing east, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請還小次，前導皇帝行，宮縣樂作。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he return to the small tent and led the emperor ahead; palace music began.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to return to the small tent and led him there as palace music began.

sentences.zh: 將至小次，禮儀使奏請釋鎮圭，殿中監跪受，皇帝入小次，簾降，樂止。

translations.literal: As they were about to reach the small tent, the ritual commissioner reported requesting that he release the tablet scepter; the Director of the Palace Department knelt and received it; the emperor entered the small tent, the curtain was lowered, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Near the small tent the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to release the tablet scepter; the Director of the Palace Department knelt to receive it as the emperor entered the small tent, the curtain lowered, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 六曰進饌。

translations.literal: Sixth, presentation of offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: presentation of offerings.

sentences.zh: 皇帝祼將畢，光祿卿詣饌殿視饌，復位。

translations.literal: As the emperor's libation was nearly finished, the Director of Palace Delicacies went to the offering hall to inspect the offerings and returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's libation neared its end, the Director of Palace Delicacies inspected the offerings in the offering hall and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 太官令率齋郎詣饌幕，以牲體設於盤，各對舉以行，自南神門入。

translations.literal: The Director of the Grand Food Service led the fast-day officers to the offering curtain, set the victim flesh on platters, each pair lifting and proceeding, and entered by the Southern Spirit Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Grand Food Service led fast-day officers to the offering curtain, set victim flesh on platters, and entered in pairs through the Southern Spirit Gate.

sentences.zh: 司徒出迎饌，宮縣樂作，奏無射宮《嘉成之曲》。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education went out to welcome the offerings; palace music began, performing in the wushe mode the piece "Fine Accomplishment."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education went out to welcome the offerings; palace music began, performing "Fine Accomplishment" in wushe mode.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒、齋郎奉饌升自太階，由正門入。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the Minister of Education and the fast-day officers bearing the offerings to ascend by the main steps and enter by the main gate.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the Minister of Education and fast-day officers bearing offerings up the main steps and in through the main gate.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝迎於階上，各跪奠於神座前。

translations.literal: The chief sacrifiers welcomed them on the steps; each knelt and set offerings before the spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: Chief sacrifiers met them on the steps; each knelt and set offerings before the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 齋郎執笏俯伏興，遍奠訖，樂止。

translations.literal: The fast-day officers held their tablets, prostrated themselves and rose; when all had been set in turn, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Fast-day officers held their tablets, prostrated and rose; when all offerings had been set, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒、太官令率齋郎降自東階，各復位。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the Minister of Education and the Director of the Grand Food Service, who led the fast-day officers, to descend by the eastern steps; each returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the Minister of Education and the Director of the Grand Food Service, with fast-day officers, down the eastern steps to their posts.

sentences.zh: 饌之升殿也，太官丞率七祀齋郎奉饌，以序跪奠於七祀神座前，退從殿上齋郎以次復位。

translations.literal: As the offerings were being brought up the hall, the assistant director of the grand food service led fast-day officers for the seven sacrifices to bear offerings, and in order knelt and set them before the spirit seats of the seven sacrifices; they withdrew and followed the hall fast-day officers in order back to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: As offerings ascended the hall, the assistant director led fast-day officers for the seven sacrifices to set offerings before their spirit seats in order, then withdraw and follow the hall officers back to their posts.

sentences.zh: 諸太官令率割牲官詣各室，進割牲體置俎上，皆退。

translations.literal: Each director of the grand food service led the officers who cut the victims to each chamber, advanced cut victim flesh and set it on the offering tables, and all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of the grand food service led cutters to each chamber to place cut flesh on the offering tables, then all withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七曰酌獻。

translations.literal: Seventh, pouring the offering.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: pouring the offering.

sentences.zh: 禮直官於殿上贊太祝立茅苴，禮儀使奏請詣盥洗位。

translations.literal: On the hall a ritual officer heralded that the chief sacrifiers should set up the divination grass; the ritual commissioner reported requesting that he proceed to the hand-washing post.
translations.idiomatic: On the hall a ritual officer called for the chief sacrifiers to set up the divination grass; the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to proceed to the hand-washing post.

sentences.zh: 簾卷，出次，宮縣樂作。

translations.literal: The curtain was rolled up; he left the tent; palace music began.
translations.idiomatic: The curtain rolled up; the emperor left the tent as palace music began.

sentences.zh: 殿中監跪進鎮圭，皇帝執鎮圭至盥洗位，樂止，北向立。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Department knelt and advanced the tablet scepter; the emperor took the tablet scepter and reached the hand-washing post; the music ceased, and he stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Palace Department knelt and presented the tablet scepter; the emperor took it to the hand-washing post, where the music ceased, and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請搢鎮圭，執事者跪取醿，興，沃水，又跪取盤，承水。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor insert the tablet scepter; an attendant knelt, took the ewer, rose, and poured water; again he knelt, took the basin, and received the water.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to set aside the tablet scepter; an attendant knelt with the ewer and poured water into a basin.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇帝盥手，執事者跪取巾於篚，興，進。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor wash his hands; an attendant knelt, took a cloth from the hamper, rose, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to wash his hands; an attendant knelt, took a cloth from the hamper, rose, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 帨手訖，禮儀使奏請執鎮圭，請詣爵洗位，北向立。

translations.literal: When drying the hands was finished, the ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take up the tablet scepter and proceed to the goblet-washing post, standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: When his hands were dried, the ritual commissioner asked him to take up the tablet scepter and go to the goblet-washing post, facing north.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請搢鎮圭，奉爵官以爵跪進。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor insert the tablet scepter; the officer bearing the goblet knelt and advanced the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to set aside the tablet scepter; the officer bearing the goblet knelt and presented it.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受爵，執事者奉醿沃水，奉盤承水。

translations.literal: The emperor received the goblet; attendants bore the ewer and poured water, and bore the basin to receive the water.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the goblet while attendants poured water from the ewer and caught it in a basin.

sentences.zh: 皇帝洗爵訖，執事者奉巾跪進。

translations.literal: When the emperor had finished washing the goblet, attendants knelt and presented the cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had washed the goblet, attendants knelt and presented the drying cloth.

sentences.zh: 皇帝拭爵，執事者奠盤醿，又奠巾於篚，奉爵官受爵。

translations.literal: The emperor wiped the goblet; attendants set down the basin and ewer, again set the cloth in the hamper, and the officer bearing the goblet received the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wiped the goblet; attendants set down basin and ewer, returned the cloth to the hamper, and the goblet-bearer received the goblet.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執鎮圭，升殿。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take up the tablet scepter and ascend the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take up the tablet scepter and ascend the hall.

sentences.zh: 宮縣樂作，至西階下，樂止。

translations.literal: Palace music began; when they reached the foot of the western steps, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Palace music played until they reached the foot of the western steps, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 升自西階，登歌樂作，禮儀使前導詣太祖室尊彜所，東向立，樂止。

translations.literal: He ascended by the western steps; ascent music began; the ritual commissioner led ahead to the ritual vessels of the Taizu chamber, standing facing east, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the western steps to ascent music; the ritual commissioner led him to the Taizu chamber vessels, facing east, and the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請搢鎮圭執爵，奉爵官以爵跪進。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor insert the tablet scepter and take the goblet; the officer bearing the goblet knelt and advanced the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to set aside the tablet scepter and take the goblet; the goblet-bearer knelt and presented it.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受爵，司尊者舉冪，良醞令跪酌犧尊之泛齊，以爵授執事者。

translations.literal: The emperor received the goblet; the Keeper of Vessels lifted the veil; the Director of Fine Brew knelt and poured the first fermentation from the sacrificial vessel and handed the goblet to an attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the goblet; the Keeper of Vessels raised the veil; the Director of Fine Brew knelt, poured the first fermentation from the sacrificial vessel, and handed the goblet to an attendant.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執鎮圭，皇帝執圭，入詣太祖神位前，北向立。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take up the tablet scepter; the emperor took the scepter, entered, and proceeded to the spirit seat of Taizu, standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take up the tablet scepter; the emperor took it, entered, and stood before Taizu's spirit seat, facing north.

sentences.zh: 宮縣樂作，奏《開成之曲》。

translations.literal: Palace music began, performing the piece "Opening Accomplishment."
translations.idiomatic: Palace music began, performing "Opening Accomplishment."

sentences.zh: 禮儀使跪奏請搢鎮圭跪，又奏請三上香。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner knelt and reported requesting that the emperor insert the tablet scepter and kneel, and again reported requesting three offerings of incense.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner knelt and asked the emperor to set aside the tablet scepter and kneel, then asked for three offerings of incense.

sentences.zh: 三上香訖，奉爵官以爵授進酒官，進酒官東向以爵跪進。

translations.literal: When the three offerings of incense were finished, the officer bearing the goblet handed the goblet to the wine-presenting officer; the wine-presenting officer faced east and knelt to advance the goblet.
translations.idiomatic: After three offerings of incense, the goblet-bearer handed the goblet to the wine-presenting officer, who faced east and knelt to present it.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執爵，三祭酒於茅苴，以虛爵授進酒官，進酒官以授奉爵官，奉爵官退立尊彜所。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take the goblet and thrice offer wine on the divination grass; he handed the empty goblet to the wine-presenting officer, who handed it to the officer bearing the goblet, and the officer bearing the goblet withdrew and stood at the ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take the goblet and thrice pour wine on the divination grass, then return the empty goblet through the wine-presenting officer to the goblet-bearer, who withdrew to the ritual vessels.

sentences.zh: 進酒官進取神案上所奠玉爵馬湩，東向跪進，禮儀使奏請執爵祭馬湩。

translations.literal: The wine-presenting officer advanced, took the jade goblet of horse milk wine set on the spirit table, faced east and knelt to advance it; the ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take the goblet and offer the horse milk wine.
translations.idiomatic: The wine-presenting officer took the jade goblet of horse-milk wine from the spirit table, faced east and knelt to present it; the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take the goblet and offer the horse-milk wine.

sentences.zh: 祭訖，以虛爵授進酒官，進酒官進奠神案上，退。

translations.literal: When the offering was finished, he handed the empty goblet to the wine-presenting officer; the wine-presenting officer advanced and set it on the spirit table and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the offering was finished he returned the empty goblet; the wine-presenting officer set it on the spirit table and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執圭，俯伏興，司徒搢笏跪於俎前，奉牲西向以進。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take up the scepter and prostrate himself and rise; the Minister of Education inserted his tablet and knelt before the offering table, bearing the victim facing west to advance it.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take up the scepter and prostrate and rise; the Minister of Education inserted his tablet, knelt before the offering table, and bore the victim facing west to present it.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請搢鎮圭，皇帝搢圭，俯受牲盤，北向跪奠神案上。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor insert the tablet scepter; the emperor inserted the scepter, bowed to receive the victim platter, and knelt facing north to set it on the spirit table.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to set aside the tablet scepter; the emperor did so, bowed to receive the victim platter, and knelt facing north to set it on the spirit table.

sentences.zh: 蒙古祝史致辭訖，禮儀使奏請執鎮圭興，前導，出戶外褥位，北向立，樂止。

translations.literal: When the Mongol prayer officer had finished his invocation, the ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take up the tablet scepter and rise, led ahead, and went out to the cushion outside the door, standing facing north; the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mongol prayer officer had finished his invocation, the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take up the tablet scepter and rise, led him to the cushion outside the door, and stood facing north as the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 舉祝官搢笏跪，對舉祝版，讀祝官北向跪，讀祝文訖，俯伏興，舉祝官奠祝版訖，先詣次室。

translations.literal: The officer who raised the prayer tablet inserted his tablet and knelt, raising the prayer tablet together; the officer who read the prayer knelt facing north, read the prayer text, then prostrated himself and rose; the officer who raised the prayer tablet set down the prayer tablet; when finished, he first proceeded to the next chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The officer raising the prayer tablet inserted his tablet and knelt, lifting the tablet with the reader; the reader knelt north-facing, read the prayer, then prostrated and rose; the raiser set down the tablet and went first to the next chamber.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請再拜。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting another bow.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked for another bow.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，禮儀使前導詣各室，各奏本室之樂。

translations.literal: When the bow was finished, the ritual commissioner led ahead to each chamber; at each chamber the music of that chamber was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the bow was finished, the ritual commissioner led him to each chamber in turn, with that chamber's music performed at each.

sentences.zh: 其酌獻、進牲、祭馬湩，並如第一室之儀。

translations.literal: The libation presentation, advancing the victim, and offering the horse-milk wine all followed the rite of the first chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The libation presentation, advancing the victim, and offering horse-milk wine all followed the same rite as in the first chamber.

sentences.zh: 既畢，禮儀使奏請詣飲福位。

translations.literal: When this was finished, the ritual commissioner reported requesting that he proceed to the blessing-drinking post.
translations.idiomatic: When this was finished, the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to proceed to the blessing-drinking post.

sentences.zh: 登歌樂作，至位，西向立，樂止。

translations.literal: Ascent music began; when he reached the post he stood facing west, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music began; at the post he stood facing west as the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 登歌《釐成之樂》作，禮直官引司徒立於飲福位側，太祝以爵酌上尊飲福酒，合置一爵，以奉侍中，侍中受爵，奉以立。

translations.literal: Ascent music, "Blessing Accomplished," began; a ritual officer led the Minister of Education to stand beside the blessing-drinking post; the Grand Supplicator filled the highest-grade blessing wine with a goblet, combined and set them in one goblet, and presented it to the attendant grandee; the attendant grandee received the goblet and stood holding it.
translations.idiomatic: Ascent music, "Blessing Accomplished," began; ritual officers led the Minister of Education to stand beside the blessing-drinking post; the Grand Supplicator poured highest-grade blessing wine into a goblet, combined it into a single cup, and presented it to the attendant grandee, who received it and stood holding it.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇帝再拜。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to bow twice.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，奏請搢鎮圭跪。

translations.literal: When the bow was finished, he reported requesting that the emperor set aside the tablet scepter and kneel.
translations.idiomatic: When the bow was finished, he asked the emperor to set aside the tablet scepter and kneel.

sentences.zh: 侍中東向以爵跪進，禮儀使奏請執爵，三祭酒，又奏請啐酒。

translations.literal: The attendant grandee faced east and knelt to advance the goblet; the ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take the goblet, thrice offer wine, and again reported requesting that he sip the wine.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant grandee faced east, knelt, and presented the goblet; the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take the goblet, thrice pour wine, then sip the wine.

sentences.zh: 啐酒訖，以爵授侍中。

translations.literal: When sipping the wine was finished, he handed the goblet to the attendant grandee.
translations.idiomatic: After sipping the wine he returned the goblet to the attendant grandee.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請受胙，太祝以黍稷飯籩授司徒，司徒東向跪進。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he receive the sacrificial portion; the Grand Supplicator handed the millet-and-grain rice basket to the Minister of Education, who knelt facing east to advance it.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to receive the sacrificial portion; the Grand Supplicator handed the millet-and-grain rice basket to the Minister of Education, who knelt east-facing to present it.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受，以授左右。

translations.literal: The emperor received it and handed it to attendants at his sides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received it and handed it to attendants.

sentences.zh: 太祝又以胙肉俎跪授司徒，司徒跪進。

translations.literal: The Grand Supplicator also knelt and handed the sacrificial-meat platter to the Minister of Education, who knelt to advance it.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Supplicator also knelt and handed the sacrificial-meat platter to the Minister of Education, who knelt to present it.

sentences.zh: 皇帝受，以授左右。

translations.literal: The emperor received it and handed it to attendants at his sides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received it and handed it to attendants.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引司徒退立。

translations.literal: A ritual officer led the Minister of Education to withdraw and stand.
translations.idiomatic: A ritual officer led the Minister of Education back to his place.

sentences.zh: 侍中再以爵酒跪進，禮儀使奏請皇帝受爵飲福。

translations.literal: The attendant grandee again knelt to advance the blessing wine in the goblet; the ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor receive the goblet and drink the blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant grandee again knelt with the blessing wine; the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take the goblet and drink the blessing.

sentences.zh: 飲福訖，侍中受虛爵，興，以授太祝。

translations.literal: When drinking the blessing was finished, the attendant grandee received the empty goblet, rose, and handed it to the Grand Supplicator.
translations.idiomatic: After drinking the blessing, the attendant grandee took the empty goblet, rose, and handed it to the Grand Supplicator.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請執鎮圭，俯伏興，又奏請再拜。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he take up the tablet scepter, prostrate himself and rise, and again reported requesting another bow.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to take up the tablet scepter, prostrate and rise, then bow again.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the bow was finished, the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When the bow was finished, the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使前導還版位，登歌樂作，降自西階，樂止。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner led ahead back to the spirit-tablet seat; ascent music began; he descended by the western steps, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner led him back to the spirit-tablet seat to ascent music; he descended the western steps as the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 宮縣樂作，至位樂止。

translations.literal: Palace music began; when he reached his seat the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Palace music played until he reached his seat.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請還小次，宮縣樂作。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he return to the small tent; palace music began.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to return to the small tent as palace music began.

sentences.zh: 將至小次，禮儀使奏請釋鎮圭，殿中監跪受。

translations.literal: When he was about to reach the small tent, the ritual commissioner reported requesting that he release the tablet scepter; the Director of the Palace Department knelt to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Approaching the small tent, the ritual commissioner asked the emperor to release the tablet scepter, and the Director of the Palace Department knelt to receive it.

sentences.zh: 入小次，簾降，樂止。

translations.literal: He entered the small tent, the curtain was lowered, and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the small tent, the curtain dropped, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 文舞退，武舞進。

translations.literal: The civil dance withdrew; the martial dance advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The civil dance withdrew and the martial dance entered.

sentences.zh: 先是皇帝酌獻訖，將至小次，禮直官引亞獻官詣盥洗位。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor had finished the libation presentation and was about to reach the small tent, a ritual officer led the second-presenting officer to the hand-washing post.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor had finished his libation and was nearing the small tent, ritual officers led the second presenter to the hand-washing post.

sentences.zh: 盥洗訖，升自阼階，酌獻並如常儀。

translations.literal: When hand-washing was finished, he ascended by the eastern steps; the libation presentation all followed the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: After washing, he ascended the eastern steps and performed the libation presentation as usual.

sentences.zh: 酌獻訖，禮直官引亞獻官詣東序，西向立。

translations.literal: When the libation presentation was finished, a ritual officer led the second-presenting officer to the eastern side hall, where he stood facing west.
translations.idiomatic: When the libation was finished, ritual officers led the second presenter to the east gallery, facing west.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝各以酌罍福酒，合置一爵，一太祝捧爵進亞獻之左，北向立。

translations.literal: Each of the Grand Supplicators poured blessing wine from the pouring jars, combined and set them in one goblet; one Grand Supplicator held the goblet and advanced to the left of the second presenter, standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Supplicators poured blessing wine from the jars into one goblet; one bore it to the second presenter's left and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 亞獻再拜受爵，跪祭酒，遂啐飲。

translations.literal: The second presenter bowed twice, received the goblet, knelt and offered wine, then sipped and drank.
translations.idiomatic: The second presenter bowed twice, received the goblet, knelt to pour wine, then sipped and drank.

sentences.zh: 太祝進受爵，退，復於坫上。

translations.literal: The Grand Supplicator advanced, received the goblet, withdrew, and restored it on the stand.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Supplicator took the goblet back and returned it to the stand.

sentences.zh: 亞獻興再拜，禮直官引亞獻官降復位。

translations.literal: The second presenter rose and bowed twice; a ritual officer led the second-presenting officer down to resume his place.
translations.idiomatic: The second presenter rose, bowed twice, and was led down to his place.

sentences.zh: 終獻如亞獻之儀。

translations.literal: The final presentation followed the rite of the second presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The final presentation followed the same rite.

sentences.zh: 初終獻既升，禮直官引七祀獻官各詣盥洗位，搢笏盥帨訖，執笏詣神位，搢笏跪執爵，三祭酒，奠爵執笏，俯伏興，再拜訖，詣次位，如上儀。

translations.literal: When the final presentation had first ascended, ritual officers led each of the seven-sacrifice presenting officers to the hand-washing post; they inserted their tablets, washed and dried their hands, took up their tablets, proceeded to the spirit seats, inserted their tablets, knelt and took the goblets, thrice offered wine, set down the goblets and took up their tablets, prostrated themselves and rose; when the bow was finished they proceeded to the next post as in the protocol above.
translations.idiomatic: When the final presenter had first ascended, ritual officers led each seven-sacrifice presenting officer to wash; they inserted their tablets, washed and dried their hands, then proceeded to each spirit seat, knelt, thrice poured wine, set down the goblets, prostrated and rose, bowed twice, and moved to the next post by the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 終獻畢，贊者唱「太祝徹籩豆」。

translations.literal: When the final presentation was finished, the herald called, "Grand Supplicator, remove the baskets and platters."
translations.idiomatic: When the final presentation was finished, the herald called, "Grand Supplicator, remove the baskets and platters."

sentences.zh: 諸太祝進徹籩豆，登歌《豐成之樂》作，卒徹樂止。

translations.literal: The Grand Supplicators advanced and removed the baskets and platters; ascent music, "Abundant Accomplishment," began; when removal was complete the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Supplicators removed the baskets and platters to ascent music, "Abundant Accomplishment," which ceased when the removal was complete.

sentences.zh: 奉禮曰「賜胙」，贊者唱「眾官再拜」，在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The ceremonial attendant said, "Bestow the sacrificial portion"; the herald called, "All officers, bow twice"; all those in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: A ceremonial attendant announced, "Bestow the sacrificial portion"; the herald called for all officers to bow twice, and all in attendance did so.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請詣版位。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he proceed to the spirit-tablet seat.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to proceed to the spirit-tablet seat.

sentences.zh: 簾卷，出次，殿中監跪進鎮圭。

translations.literal: The curtain was rolled up; he left the tent; the Director of the Palace Department knelt and advanced the tablet scepter.
translations.idiomatic: The curtain rose; he left the tent; and the Director of the Palace Department knelt to present the tablet scepter.

sentences.zh: 皇帝執圭行，宮縣樂作，至位樂止。

translations.literal: The emperor took the scepter and walked; palace music began; when he reached his seat the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the scepter and walked to palace music, which ceased at his seat.

sentences.zh: 送神《保成之樂》作，一成止。

translations.literal: Music for sending off the spirits, "Preserving Accomplishment," began; one movement and it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Music for sending off the spirits, "Preserving Accomplishment," played one movement and stopped.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請皇帝再拜，贊者承傳，凡在位者皆再拜。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that the emperor bow twice; the herald transmitted the call; all those in attendance bowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to bow twice; the herald relayed the call, and everyone present bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使前奏禮畢，前導皇帝還大次。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner advanced and reported that the rite was complete, and led the emperor ahead back to the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner announced the rite complete and led the emperor back to the great tent.

sentences.zh: 宮縣《昌寧之樂》作，出門樂止。

translations.literal: Palace music, "Flourishing Peace," began; when he passed out the gate the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Palace music, "Flourishing Peace," played until he passed out the gate.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使奏請釋鎮圭，殿中監跪受，華蓋傘扇引導如常儀。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner reported requesting that he release the tablet scepter; the Director of the Palace Department knelt to receive it; canopy, parasol, and fan escort led as in the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commissioner asked the emperor to release the tablet scepter; the Director of the Palace Department knelt to receive it; and the canopy escort proceeded as usual.

sentences.zh: 入大次，簾降。

translations.literal: He entered the great tent and the curtain was lowered.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the great tent and the curtain dropped.

sentences.zh: 禮直官引太常卿、御史、太廟令、太祝、宮闈令升殿納神主，降就拜位，奉禮贊升納神主訖，再拜，御史以下諸執事者皆再拜，以次出。

translations.literal: Ritual officers led the Minister of Court Ceremonies, the censor, the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Grand Supplicator, and the Director of the Palace Gates to ascend the hall and install the spirit tablets; they descended to their bowing posts; the ceremonial attendant heralded that installation of the spirit tablets was finished; they bowed twice; all attending officers from the censor downward bowed twice and withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the Minister of Court Ceremonies, the censor, the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Grand Supplicator, and the Director of the Palace Gates to ascend and install the spirit tablets, then descend to their bowing posts; a ceremonial attendant announced the installation complete; they bowed twice, as did all attending officers from the censor down, and withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 禮直官各引享官以次出，太樂令率工人二舞以次出，太廟令闔戶以降乃退。

translations.literal: Ritual officers each led the officers attending the sacrifice to withdraw in order; the Director of the Imperial Music Office led the two dance companies of workers to withdraw in order; the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple closed the doors and only then descended and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers led the sacrifice officers out in order; the Director of the Imperial Music Office led both dance companies out; the Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple closed the doors and only then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 祝冊藏於匱。

translations.literal: The prayer tablets were stored in the casket.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer tablets were placed in the casket.

sentences.zh: 八曰車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Eighth, the imperial carriage returns to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: the imperial carriage returns to the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇帝既還大次，侍中奏請解嚴。

translations.literal: When the emperor had returned to the great tent, the attendant grandee reported requesting that the vigil be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to the great tent, the attendant grandee asked to dismiss the vigil.

sentences.zh: 皇帝釋袞冕，停大次。

translations.literal: The emperor removed the ceremonial crown and robe and remained in the great tent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed his ceremonial robes and remained in the great tent.

sentences.zh: 五刻頃，尚食進膳。

translations.literal: At about the fifth quarter-hour mark, the Director of Food presented the meal.
translations.idiomatic: About a quarter-hour later, the Director of Food brought the meal.

sentences.zh: 所司備法駕鹵簿，與侍祠官序立於太廟欞星門外，以北為上。

translations.literal: The responsible offices prepared the statutory guard of honor and insignia; together with the officers attending the sacrifice they stood in order outside the Lattice Star Gate of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, with north as the place of honor.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices prepared the statutory guard of honor; officers attending the sacrifice lined up outside the Imperial Ancestral Temple's Lattice Star Gate, north being the position of honor.

sentences.zh: 侍中版奏請中嚴，皇帝改服通天冠、絳紗袍。

translations.literal: The attendant grandee reported by placard requesting the inner vigil; the emperor changed into the Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant grandee reported by placard for the inner vigil; the emperor changed into his Tongtian crown and crimson gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 少頃，侍中版奏皇帝出次升輿，導駕官前導，華蓋傘扇如儀。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, the attendant grandee reported by placard that the emperor left the tent and mounted the palanquin; escort officers led ahead; canopy, parasol, and fan were as in the protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, the attendant grandee reported that the emperor left the tent and mounted the palanquin with the prescribed canopy escort.

sentences.zh: 至廟門外，太僕卿率其屬進金輅如式。

translations.literal: When they reached outside the temple gate, the Minister of the Imperial Stud led his subordinates to advance the golden carriage as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: At the temple gate, the Minister of the Imperial Stud and his staff brought up the golden carriage as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 侍中前奏請皇帝降輿升輅。

translations.literal: The attendant grandee advanced and reported requesting that the emperor descend from the palanquin and mount the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant grandee asked the emperor to leave the palanquin and mount the carriage.

sentences.zh: 升輅訖，太僕禦。

translations.literal: When mounting the carriage was finished, the Minister of the Imperial Stud took the reins.
translations.idiomatic: Once mounted, the Minister of the Imperial Stud took the reins.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎奉請車駕進發，俯伏興，退。

translations.literal: The vice minister of the Gate Department, bearing the request, asked that the imperial carriage set out; he prostrated himself and rose and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister of the Gate Department asked the carriage to depart, then prostrated, rose, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 車駕動，稱警蹕。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage moved; the cry "Halt the way!" was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage moved and the cry to clear the way was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 至欞星門外，門下侍郎奉請車駕權停，敕眾官上馬。

translations.literal: When they reached outside the Lattice Star Gate, the vice minister of the Gate Department, bearing the request, asked that the imperial carriage halt briefly and commanded all officers to mount their horses.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Lattice Star Gate the vice minister asked the carriage to halt briefly and ordered all officers to mount.

sentences.zh: 侍中承旨退稱曰「制可」。

translations.literal: The attendant grandee received the edict, withdrew, and proclaimed, "The command is approved."
translations.idiomatic: The attendant grandee received the edict and proclaimed, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎退傳制，贊者承傳。

translations.literal: The vice minister of the Gate Department withdrew and transmitted the command; the herald transmitted it in relay.
translations.idiomatic: The vice minister withdrew and relayed the command; heralds passed it on.

sentences.zh: 眾官上馬畢，門下侍郎奏請敕車右升。

translations.literal: When all officers had finished mounting, the vice minister of the Gate Department reported requesting the command that the right-hand rider of the carriage mount.
translations.idiomatic: When all had mounted, the vice minister asked permission for the carriage guard to mount.

sentences.zh: 侍中承旨退稱「制可」，千牛將軍升訖，導駕官分左右前導，門下侍郎奏請車駕進發。

translations.literal: The attendant grandee received the edict, withdrew, and proclaimed, "The command is approved"; when the Thousand-Ox General had finished mounting, escort officers led left and right ahead; the vice minister of the Gate Department reported requesting that the imperial carriage set out.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant grandee received the edict and proclaimed, "Approved"; once the Thousand-Ox General had mounted, escort officers led left and right ahead, and the vice minister asked the carriage to depart.

sentences.zh: 車駕動，稱警蹕。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage moved; the cry "Halt the way!" was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage moved and the cry to clear the way was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎奉八寶與殿中監從，教坊樂鼓吹振作。

translations.literal: The Keeper of Seals bore the eight treasures and followed with the Director of the Palace Department; the Music Bureau's drums and pipes sounded vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: The Keeper of Seals bore the eight treasures with the Director of the Palace Department; Music Bureau drums and pipes sounded vigorously.

sentences.zh: 駕至崇天門外垣欞星門外，門下侍郎奏請車駕權停，敕眾官下馬。

translations.literal: When the carriage reached outside the Lattice Star Gate on the outer wall of the Gate of Ascending to Heaven, the vice minister of the Gate Department reported requesting that the carriage halt briefly and commanded all officers to dismount.
translations.idiomatic: At the outer Lattice Star Gate by the Gate of Ascending to Heaven, the vice minister asked the carriage to halt and ordered all officers to dismount.

sentences.zh: 贊者承傳，眾官下馬。

translations.literal: The herald transmitted the call; all officers dismounted.
translations.idiomatic: Heralds relayed the order and all officers dismounted.

sentences.zh: 車駕動，眾官前引入內石橋，與儀仗倒卷而北，駐立。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage moved; all officers were led ahead into the inner stone bridge; together with the honor guard they wheeled about to face north and stood.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage moved on; officers were led ahead to the inner stone bridge, where they and the honor guard wheeled to face north and stood.

sentences.zh: 駕入崇天門，至大明門外降駕，升輿以入。

translations.literal: The carriage entered the Gate of Ascending to Heaven; when it reached outside the Gate of Great Brightness the emperor descended from the carriage and mounted the palanquin to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage entered the Gate of Ascending to Heaven; at the Gate of Great Brightness the emperor left the carriage and entered on the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 駕既入，通事舍人承旨敕眾官皆退，宿衛官率衛士宿衛如式。

translations.literal: When the carriage had entered, the Herald of Affairs received the edict and commanded that all officers withdraw; the night-guard officers led the guards in night watch as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside, the Herald of Affairs ordered all officers to withdraw; night-guard officers posted guards as prescribed.
